# Agent Workflow Guidelines

This document defines the standard workflow required for all AI coding agents
working on this codebase, and it is the single source of truth for that
workflow. Every agent reads this file. Tool-specific entrypoints such as
`CLAUDE.md` only point here — never add rules, commands, or project facts to
them, because agents that read a different entrypoint will not see them. Add it
here instead. Registered subagent definitions may describe their role and
reporting format, but they must defer project facts, gate applicability, and
verification commands to this file.

## The project

Event-driven Go microservices for reporting and matching lost pets, running on
GCP (Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, Firestore, GCS) and locally via Docker Compose plus
Ollama `gemma4:e2b`.

The repository has five services. Four expose JSON HTTP endpoints or run as
Pub/Sub workers; `web-frontend` serves rendered HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and JSON
API endpoints. The Playwright suite contains both API-level request journeys
and browser-driven page coverage.

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `cmd/` | Service entrypoints: `lostpet-service`, `foundpet-service`, `pet-matcher`, `notification-service`, `web-frontend` |
| `pkg/` | Shared packages: `domain`, `store`, `pubsub`, `outbox`, `delivery`, `blob`, `ollama`, `scoring`, `runtimeconfig`, `telemetry` |
| `e2e/` | Event-cascade tests: in-memory/test-server cascades plus emulator-gated Firestore and Pub/Sub contracts |
| `tests/playwright/` | API and browser journeys using three local HTTP services |
| `infra/opentofu/` | GCP infrastructure modules |
| `deploy/cloudrun/` | Cloud Run manifests |
| `docs/` | `DEVELOPMENT.md` |

## Code Review Rules

These rules guide local reviewers. Keep deterministic formatting, lint, build,
and test checks in the verifier and CI.

- Pub/Sub handlers must remain idempotent under redelivery. Flag writes,
  notifications, or state transitions that can be duplicated when the same
  event is delivered more than once; use a stable event or deduplication key,
  or make the operation inherently idempotent.
- Event schema changes must remain backward compatible with in-flight
  messages. Prefer additive fields with tolerant readers; otherwise introduce
  an explicit version and preserve a decoder or migration path for the prior
  schema.
- Reporter contact details and state-changing actions must not cross an
  unauthenticated or unauthorized boundary. Apply this rule to new or changed
  boundaries: return redacted public DTOs and require authentication plus
  ownership or equivalent authorization before exposing contact data or
  mutating pet and match state. Existing pre-authentication demo behavior is
  roadmap debt, not precedent for expanding the exposed boundary.
- Automated tests must exercise product code or product behavior. Do not add
  tests that inspect repository files such as documentation, agent guidance,
  CI workflows, dependency metadata, Docker or deployment manifests, or
  OpenTofu source. Validate those artifacts with their native lint, build,
  configuration, or validation commands instead.

## Ground rules

These apply at every step, not just at the gate where they are mentioned.

- **Never commit directly to `main`.** Never force-push, never amend or rebase
  a commit that has already been pushed, and never discard user work with
  `git checkout --`, `git restore`, `git clean`, or `git reset --hard`.
- **Preserve unrelated work.** Staged, unstaged, and untracked files that you
  did not create belong to the user. Leave them alone.
- **Never commit secrets.** No service-account JSON, `*.tfstate`, `.env` files,
  API keys, or real GCP project identifiers. If you need a credential to
  proceed, stop and ask.
- **Stop and ask the user** rather than pushing through when: a gate fails
  twice for the same reason; the task requires a credential, a paid resource,
  or a destructive operation; the change would alter published API contracts,
  infrastructure state, or CI enforcement; or the request is ambiguous enough
  that two readings produce materially different work.

## Workflow

1. **Inspect before changing anything.** Inspect the repository, current Git
   state, and all applicable instruction files before making changes.

2. **Choose a thin vertical slice.** Before implementing a tracked issue or
   feature, define the smallest end-to-end slice that can be reviewed, tested,
   shipped, and merged independently. Prefer one coherent user-visible or
   operational outcome over a broad horizontal layer. If the next issue is too
   large for one pull request, split it into ordered slices and complete only
   the current slice. Keep pull requests small enough for thorough review,
   reliable verification, and quick rollback.

3. **Create a branch for that slice.** Branch from the latest `main` using
   `<type>/<short-kebab-summary>`, where `<type>` is one of `feat`, `fix`,
   `refactor`, `chore`, `test`, or `docs` — matching the Conventional Commit
   type the work will land under. Example: `feat/foundpet-image-upload`.

4. **Use test-driven development when behavior or structure is testable.**
   - Add or update a focused test before implementation.
   - Run it and confirm it fails for the expected reason.
   - Implement the smallest appropriate change.
   - Run focused tests while iterating.
   - Refactor only while the relevant tests remain green.
   - Follow [Test execution ownership](#test-execution-ownership) so the main
     agent retains only focused Go test output and the verifier owns noisy or
     repository-wide execution.

5. **Inspect the complete diff and track out-of-scope discoveries.** Review the
   branch diff plus all staged, unstaged, and untracked files. Remove
   accidental or unrelated changes while preserving work that belongs to the
   user. Whenever you discover bugs, technical debt, missing features, or
   refactoring opportunities not aligned with the current slice, file them with
   `gh issue create` rather than expanding scope. Title them as Conventional
   Commits, label them `agent-found`, and reference the branch that surfaced
   them. Filing these issues is pre-authorized; you do not need to ask first.

6. **Run `ui-review` when the change can affect rendered UI.** Invoke the
   `ui-review` sub-agent after an implementation pass. See
   [Applicability](#applicability) for when this gate is live. When it applies,
   exercise the changed journey in the rendered application at representative
   phone, tablet, and desktop viewports; inspect interaction, loading, empty,
   error, focus, keyboard, contrast, and responsive states; and capture
   screenshots or equivalent visual evidence. Address every actionable finding
   before running the `verifier`. When the change has no UI impact, record one
   line stating that and move on — do not fabricate a review.

   Bring the rendered app up with `docker compose up --build -d web-frontend`
   (port 8082; it needs neither Ollama nor the other services), then stop only
   what you started with `docker compose rm -sf web-frontend` — a project-wide
   `down` would tear down a stack the user or an earlier step is using. The `-d`
   spelling is deliberate: it keeps this line from colliding with the guarded
   `--detach` stack command in [Verification scope](#verification-scope).
   Starting the app so the gate can run is not test execution, so the Compose
   restriction in [Test execution ownership](#test-execution-ownership) does not
   apply to it.

7. **Run `verifier` before code review.** Invoke the `verifier` sub-agent to run
   the builds, static checks, tests, and journey coverage appropriate for the
   change. The verifier must report failures, flakes, missing coverage, and
   environment issues, and must state explicitly which suites it could not run
   and why (for example, the local HTTP services required by Playwright could
   not be started). Fix or explicitly resolve every actionable finding before
   starting code review. If a verifier finding requires a code change, rerun
   the verifier after addressing it. A focused-support verifier run during TDD
   does not satisfy this gate; invoke the verifier fresh against the settled
   worktree for the complete applicable battery.

8. **Run the local `code-review` before every commit.** Invoke the
    `code-review` sub-agent against the current branch diff and every staged,
    unstaged, and untracked file. Address every actionable finding before
    committing. If review findings cause changes, rerun the affected tests and
    the `verifier`, then obtain a fresh `code-review` approval for the changed
    state.

9. **Commit after approval.** Commit only after verification and code review are
   complete. Use Conventional Commits:

   ```text
   <type>(<scope>): <imperative summary>
   ```

   Keep the subject at 72 characters or fewer, describe why in the body when
   useful, and do not combine unrelated work.

10. **Create pull requests from the reviewed state.**
    - Confirm that local verification remains valid.
    - Rerun `code-review` only if the reviewed state changed after the
      pre-commit review. A changed state includes code, tests, documentation,
      generated files, conflict resolution, or any other staged, unstaged, or
      untracked content. Do not repeat code review when the already-reviewed
      diff and worktree remain unchanged.
    - Title the pull request as a Conventional Commit. CI enforces this, and
      because short-lived branches are squash-merged, the pull request title
      becomes the commit subject on `main`.
    - Link the tracked issue in the pull request body: `Closes #<n>` only when
      this slice completes the issue, `Part of #<n>` for every earlier slice of
      an ordered split. The squash merge carries the body onto `main`, so
      `Closes` on an intermediate slice closes the issue while later slices are
      still outstanding.
    - Push and open a normal, ready-for-review pull request. Do not open draft
      pull requests unless the user explicitly asks for a draft.

11. **Merge only clean, passing pull requests.** Merge only after GitHub reports
    a clean merge state and every configured check passes. Never bypass a
    failing or pending required check. Self-merges are allowed when these
    conditions are met. Use squash merge for short-lived development branches to
    keep `main` linear, then delete the merged branch.

## Gate discipline

The `ui-review` → `verifier` → `code-review` sequence can otherwise loop
forever. It is bounded by these rules.

- **Actionable** means correctness, security, data-loss, accessibility, or
  contract defects, plus anything the sub-agent marks as blocking. Style
  preferences and speculative refactors are not actionable; note them, or file
  them per step 5, and move on.
- **Two rounds maximum.** If the same gate reports actionable findings on a
  third pass, stop and hand the disagreement to the user with both positions
  summarized.
- **Rerun only what the change invalidated.** A documentation-only fix after a
  review does not require rerunning the full verifier suite; say what you
  reran and why.
- **Never self-certify a gate.** If a sub-agent is unavailable, say so
  explicitly and state what you checked manually instead. Do not report a gate
  as passed when it did not run.

## Test execution ownership

Keep the main agent's context focused on design and implementation. Split test
execution by phase and weight:

| Phase | Main agent | `verifier` sub-agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Go TDD red/green | Writes the test and runs only the exact focused Go test, scoped by package and `-run` | Not required |
| Integration or journey TDD red/green | Writes the focused contract and interprets the concise result | Runs only the named emulator, Docker, or Playwright test in focused-support mode |
| Settled implementation gate | Does not duplicate the full battery | Starts fresh and runs every applicable command in [Verification scope](#verification-scope) |

The main agent may rerun a tightly related set of named Go tests while
refactoring, but it does not run repository-wide tests, race/coverage, lint,
Compose rebuilds, emulator batteries, infrastructure validation, or
Playwright — the one exception being the single-service `ui-review` bring-up in
step 6, which starts the app rather than running tests. A focused Go test
already compiles its package; do not add a broad build merely to prove
compilation during the TDD loop.

All automated Playwright execution belongs to the verifier, including a single
spec or test selected for journey TDD. In focused-support mode, the verifier
reports the command, the red or green result, and the decisive failure evidence
without claiming the formal gate. After the implementation settles, use a
fresh verifier invocation for the full applicable suite. Manual viewport and
accessibility inspection remains the separate `ui-review` responsibility.

## Applicability

Not every gate applies to every change. Record the reason when one does not.

| Gate | Applies when | Status in this repo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ui-review` | The change affects rendered UI — templates, static assets, styling, or a client app | **Live.** Active for `cmd/web-frontend` templates, CSS, and client-side JavaScript (`static/js/`, `static/sw.js`). |
| `verifier` | Always | Live |
| `code-review` | Always | Live |

The Playwright suite in `tests/playwright/` contains both API request specs and
browser-driven page specs. The verifier owns all automated Playwright coverage;
browser specs complement but do not replace the manual, viewport-based
`ui-review` gate for rendered UI changes.

# PetSpotR Development & Deployment Guide

Welcome to the PetSpotR Go & Google Cloud Platform codebase. This document
outlines how to build, test, run locally, and deploy PetSpotR.

---

## 1. Architecture Overview

PetSpotR is an event-driven microservice system written in **Go 1.22+**:

- **`web-frontend`** (`cmd/web-frontend`): Modern web application UI at `http://localhost:8082`,
  offering Lost Pet wizards, Found Pet dropzone, AI visual match comparison dashboard, and Web Push.
- **`lostpet-service`** (`cmd/lostpet-service`): Exposes REST API
  `POST /lostPet`, persists lost pet events, and emits `lostPet` events.
- **`foundpet-service`** (`cmd/foundpet-service`): Exposes REST API
  `POST /foundPet/uploads` and `POST /foundPet`, validates private image
  uploads, persists found pet events, and emits `foundPet` events.
- **`pet-matcher`** (`cmd/pet-matcher`): Private HTTP service receiving
  authenticated `foundPet` Pub/Sub push requests, performing visual feature
  extraction using **Ollama** and **Gemma 4** models (`gemma4:e2b`), scoring
  similarity against lost pets, and emitting `matchFound` events.
- **`notification-service`** (`cmd/notification-service`): Private HTTP service
  receiving authenticated `matchFound` Pub/Sub push requests and generating
  owner alert emails, SMS, and Web Push notifications.

Cloud Run receives the bucket name from OpenTofu. Its found-pet identity has

The secure found-pet flow is:

1. `POST /foundPet/uploads` with `purpose: "found-pet"` and a JPEG or PNG
   content type. The service ignores the caller filename and returns a
   cryptographically generated report ID, temporary object name, and V4 POST
   policy fields. It also returns a separate `finalizeToken`; only its SHA-256
   digest is signed into object metadata.
2. Multipart POST the file and every returned field to `uploadUrl`. The policy
   expires after 15 minutes and binds the exact object, media type, report
   metadata, finalization deadline, and a 1 byte through 10 MiB size range.
3. `POST /foundPet` using the returned `reportId` as `petId` and temporary
   `objectName` as `imageObject`, and send the raw capability in
   `X-PetSpotR-Upload-Token`. Before creating report state or its outbox, the
   service checks the capability in constant time plus immutable GCS
   generation, size, metadata, detected media type, decoded dimensions, and
   report binding. The signed finalization deadline remains enforced after the
   object is copied, and the whole report operation has a two-minute server
   deadline. It then copies the object to the private finalized namespace and
   deletes the temporary object. The raw capability is never persisted in GCS
   metadata or the durable event.

Durable events store only the finalized object name. The matcher reads that
private object with its service identity and base64-encodes the bytes for
Ollama; no public or expiring URL is placed in an event. Private read URLs are
V4-signed and capped at 15 minutes. Existing URL events remain readable during
the schema migration, but managed found-pet report creation rejects them.

The bucket enforces public access prevention and uniform access. Set
`image_cors_allowed_origins` to exact deployed web origins; the default empty
list permits no browser origin. Unfinalized `uploads/` objects are deleted
after one day. The found-pet process also reconciles at most 100 finalized
objects per pass with a cursor. After a 24-hour grace period—well beyond the
15-minute capability and two-minute report deadlines—it deletes an object only
when two durable-state checks find no report referencing the exact name and the
object generation is unchanged. This recovers the crash window between GCS
finalization and the Firestore report transaction without deleting active,
referenced, or replaced objects. The capability authenticates the generated
report upload; tying that capability to a signed-in user remains tracked by
issue #110. Routing the browser through the canonical service remains tracked
by issue #113.

### Transactional report outbox

The lost- and found-report services create aggregate state and a durable
`eventOutbox` record in one transaction. Each outbox payload uses envelope
version 1 with a stable event ID, type, occurrence time, correlation and trace
IDs, aggregate ID and version, and payload version. Consumers accept both this
envelope and the legacy raw event payload so messages already in flight remain
readable.

An exact retry is a successful no-op and cannot reset a completed outbox
record. A competing create with the same pet ID returns `409 Conflict`; report
creation is aggregate version 1 and does not use last-write-wins ordering. Each
relay serializes publication within one process. The lost- and found-report
services poll a bounded, indexed set of their pending records every five
seconds, so failed publication stays pending across a restart and is recovered.
Before polling, a cursor-backed bounded compatibility sweep adds the query
fields missing from legacy key/data-only Firestore outbox documents. Incomplete
sweeps advance from the durable cursor. Completed sweeps restart after one
minute so a late write from an old Cloud Run revision cannot remain behind the
old cursor.

The lost- and found-report Cloud Run services temporarily run exactly one
minimum instance each with CPU available outside requests. This is required for
their five-second relays. Issue #122 owns later load/cost tuning. A crash after
broker publication but before the completion write can publish the record
again, which is the expected at-least-once boundary.

Before broker I/O, every relay instance transactionally leases the pending
outbox record for ten minutes and increments its fenced attempt. An active lease
is a successful no-op for a competing relay. Provider failure releases the
lease immediately; a process crash leaves it recoverable after expiry. Only the
winning attempt can persist completion or failure, so a stale process cannot
overwrite a newer retry. The stable event envelope lets consumers deduplicate
the unavoidable crash window after broker acceptance but before the completion
transaction.

    "body": "Surfaced while implementing issue #108 on branch `feat/foundpet-pubsub-push`.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe repository verifies with Go 1.26.5, but `Dockerfile` still builds every service with `golang:1.22-alpine`. Google Cloud Pub/Sub v2 is the current client line, but its current release requires a newer Go toolchain than the container builder. The #108 slice therefore uses the compatible `cloud.google.com/go/pubsub` v1 client, which is deprecated upstream.\n\nThis does not block the authenticated push slice, but it leaves the production image toolchain behind CI and creates avoidable future migration debt.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Pin the Docker builder to the same Go 1.26.5 toolchain used by CI and `AGENTS.md`.\n- Migrate the managed publisher and emulator contract from `cloud.google.com/go/pubsub` v1 to `cloud.google.com/go/pubsub/v2`.\n- Preserve publish acknowledgement, topic reuse, client shutdown, emulator isolation, and redelivery integration coverage.\n- Rebuild every service image and run the full verifier and Playwright gates.\n- Update dependency and development documentation without changing the `go.mod` language version unless required and explicitly reviewed.\n\nReference: branch `feat/foundpet-pubsub-push`.",

    "body": "## Problem\n\nThe public web process exposes report creation, feature extraction/inference, upload signing, push subscription/test, contact, and lifecycle mutation endpoints with no rate limiting, quota enforcement, bot friction, or request-cost controls. Per-request body limits are useful but do not prevent repeated requests, storage exhaustion, notification abuse, or expensive model invocation.\n\nSurfaced during the repository readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:60-69` registers every API directly on the public mux.\n- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:267`, `:320`, `:413`, `:582`, `:632`, `:667`, and `:730` cap individual bodies but provide no caller- or route-level request budget.\n- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:308-340` performs feature extraction on submitted image data, an expensive path once real inference is connected.\n- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:626-652` and `:724-769` expose contact and push operations without delivery-abuse controls.\n- No rate-limiter, challenge, moderation queue, Cloud Armor policy, quota middleware, or abuse telemetry exists in `cmd/`, `pkg/`, or `infra/`.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Define a threat and cost model for anonymous report, upload, inference, contact, and notification operations.\n- Apply per-IP and, after authentication, per-account quotas with stricter route-specific limits for expensive or externally billable work.\n- Add bounded concurrency and queue/backpressure controls around inference and notification delivery.\n- Require single-use, short-lived upload intents and enforce storage/object quotas.\n- Add bot/spam defenses appropriate to the public reporting journey without blocking accessibility.\n- Record privacy-safe abuse metrics and alert on rejection rate, unusual spend, inference saturation, and notification spikes.\n- Define trusted-proxy/IP handling and test header spoofing before using client IP as an identity signal.\n- Add deterministic tests for burst, sustained, concurrent, and distributed-limit behavior.\n- Provision edge controls in code if the production ingress uses an external Application Load Balancer/Cloud Armor.\n\n## Scope\n\nThis complements #110 (identity/authorization), #109 (secure upload lifecycle), #111 (AI hosting), #121 (SLOs/alerts), and #122 (cost guardrails). Those issues do not define request-level abuse prevention.",

    "body": "## Problem\n\nThe match dashboard renders persisted match fields by interpolating them into an HTML string and assigning the result to `innerHTML`. Once real reports and persisted matcher output replace the current seed data, attacker-controlled pet names, breeds, locations, image URLs, or IDs can become stored DOM injection.\n\nSurfaced during the repository readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- `cmd/web-frontend/static/js/match-dashboard.js:41` assigns concatenated match-card markup to `container.innerHTML`.\n- `cmd/web-frontend/static/js/match-dashboard.js:45-139` interpolates `matchId`, pet name, breed, location, image URL, status, and score fields into HTML, attributes, and inline styles without contextual encoding.\n- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:555-572` returns persisted match documents directly to the browser.\n- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:47-71` registers the application without a response-security-header middleware; there is no Content Security Policy to reduce impact.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Construct match cards with DOM APIs and `textContent`, or apply proven contextual encoding for text and attribute values.\n- Validate image URLs against the application-owned storage policy before assigning them to `src`.\n- Treat match IDs and numeric score/style values as typed, validated data rather than markup.\n- Add a restrictive Content Security Policy and baseline response headers without relying on CSP as the primary injection fix.\n- Remove inline script/style dependencies needed to enforce the chosen CSP.\n- Add browser tests containing HTML, quote, and script-like payloads in every rendered persisted field and assert they remain inert.\n- Cover both server-seeded/test fixtures and the future canonical persisted-match path.\n\n## Scope\n\nThis issue is distinct from #110, which covers authentication, ownership, and contact privacy. It addresses browser-side output handling and defense in depth.",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nKey interactions are mouse-only or lack accessible dialog behavior:\n\n- Upload drop zones are non-focusable `div` elements with hidden inputs and click/drop handlers only.\n- Navigation is hidden below 768px without a replacement.\n- Modals lack dialog semantics, focus trap/restore, and Escape handling.\n- Validation uses blocking `alert()` calls instead of field errors/live regions.\n- CSS has hover styling but no consistent `:focus-visible` or reduced-motion treatment.\n- Playwright defines no device projects or automated accessibility checks.\n\nClosed UI issues #50–#60 claimed WCAG/responsive coverage, but these behaviors remain.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Restore an operable mobile navigation pattern.\n- Use native file controls or make drop zones fully keyboard-operable with accessible names and announced status.\n- Add visible focus treatment and preserve logical tab order through the multi-step form.\n- Give modals correct dialog semantics, labels, focus trap/restore, Escape behavior, and background inertness.\n- Replace blocking alerts with field-associated errors and live regions.\n- Respect reduced motion and verify contrast in both themes.\n- Add automated accessibility checks and representative phone/tablet/desktop browser projects.\n- Complete the repository's manual `ui-review` gate with screenshots and keyboard evidence.\n\n## Related\n\nThis is a follow-up to the closed frontend milestone issues, not a replacement for real product data work.",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\n`status` is parsed but never applied (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:168-170,206-259,352-405`). Species is discarded on write and records without species pass a species filter. Pagination slices values collected from a Go map (`pkg/store/store.go:91-109`), whose iteration order is undefined, so page contents can duplicate or disappear between requests. Invalid query inputs silently fall back to defaults, and unknown locations silently become Seattle.\n\nClosed #93 claimed store-backed pagination and spatial filtering, but the implementation is in-memory, unstable, and only weakly tested.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Persist and enforce every documented filter.\n- Reject malformed limits, cursors, coordinates, radii, and incomplete geo parameter pairs with a clear 400 response.\n- Use a stable indexed sort with opaque cursor pagination; define tie-breaking behavior.\n- Guarantee adjacent pages cannot duplicate or omit records under a stable snapshot.\n- Treat missing/ungeocoded locations as unknown, never Seattle.\n- Return pagination metadata/links without exposing private fields.\n- Implement the same semantics in memory/emulator and Firestore adapters.\n- Add negative-filter, stable-order, insert-between-pages, boundary, and multi-page tests.\n\n## Related\n\nFollow-up to closed #61, #92, and #93; depends on #114 and Firestore indexes in #119.",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\n`cmd/pet-matcher/worker.go:60-69` passes `FoundPetEvent.ImageURL` directly in Ollama's `images` array. The Ollama API expects image data (base64 in the REST request), not an arbitrary application URL. Existing mock integration tests never validate the image payload, so this path can stay green without performing vision inference.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Resolve images only from trusted application storage using the verified object reference from #109/#114.\n- Enforce bounded size, supported MIME type, successful image decoding, and pixel/dimension limits before inference.\n- Encode image bytes in the format required by the configured Ollama API.\n- Do not allow arbitrary caller-controlled URLs or network fetches.\n- Classify corrupt image, missing object, transient inference, timeout, and invalid model-output failures.\n- Ensure logs/traces do not contain raw image bytes or signed URLs.\n- Add a payload-validating fake-Ollama integration test.\n- Add an opt-in real `gemma4:e2b` smoke test using a small licensed fixture.\n\nOfficial Ollama vision input guidance: https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/vision",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nCloud Run OpenTofu defines no concurrency, timeout, min/max instances, or resource policy (`infra/opentofu/modules/cloudrun/main.tf:1-54`). Worker manifests disable CPU throttling, and the proposed AI path can add GPU cost. No budget, forecast, anomaly, or quota alerts exist.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Load-test and set per-service CPU, memory, timeout, concurrency, min/max instances, and startup CPU settings.\n- Bound downstream pressure on Firestore, Pub/Sub, notification providers, and GPU quota.\n- Label resources for cost allocation and publish expected idle, normal, and peak monthly cost models.\n- Add actual-spend and forecast budget thresholds plus anomaly/quota notifications.\n- Define safe GPU scale-to-zero/min-instance behavior from #111 benchmarks.\n- Add a documented emergency cost-control response that preserves data integrity.\n- Revisit and record limits after staged load tests and production usage.\n\nCloud Run maximum instances: https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/max-instances\n\nCloud Billing budgets: https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nFirestore is a bare database with no deletion protection, PITR, backup schedule, TTL policy, or declared indexes (`infra/opentofu/modules/firestore/main.tf:1-5`). The image bucket sets `force_destroy=true` and enables versioning without lifecycle bounds (`infra/opentofu/modules/storage/main.tf:1-9`). Regional/multi-region, RPO, and RTO choices are undocumented.\n\nClosed #93 adds in-memory filtering, not Firestore indexes or recovery.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Decide and document regional versus multi-region Firestore before production creation.\n- Set production deletion protection, point-in-time recovery, and scheduled backups.\n- Declare required composite/geospatial/query indexes in code.\n- Set production image storage to `force_destroy=false`.\n- Choose soft-delete/versioning/lifecycle retention and cap noncurrent versions and orphan uploads.\n- Define retention for reports, matches, events, push subscriptions, and audit records.\n- Define RPO/RTO and execute documented Firestore and GCS restore drills.\n- Monitor backup failures, restore readiness, and storage growth.\n- Verify user deletion/export workflows do not destroy evidence or backups contrary to policy.\n\nFirestore backup guidance: https://cloud.google.com/firestore/docs/backups",

Documentation directs developers to apply directly from a laptop, and infra tests only assert that files/resources contain expected strings.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Add a documented bootstrap path for a private, versioned, access-controlled GCS state bucket.\n- Commit the dependency lock file and use intentionally reviewed provider constraints.\n- Separate development, staging, and production projects/roots with explicit variables, labels, and guardrails.\n- Enable required Google APIs declaratively.\n- Add CI plan output, formatting/validation, policy checks, approval-gated apply, and scheduled drift detection.\n- Use ADC and Workload Identity Federation; prohibit downloaded service-account keys.\n- Prevent accidental cross-environment plans/applies and destructive production changes.\n- Add semantic IaC tests for identities, ingress, subscriptions, deletion protection, and immutable images.\n- Document state recovery and lock/concurrency procedures.\n\nGoogle Terraform security practices: https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/terraform/best-practices/security",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\n`docker compose up --build` starts isolated service containers plus Ollama, but no shared state or event transport (`docker-compose.yml:28-84`). The Go cascade tests share one in-process memory broker; Playwright starts only lost, found, and web services and checks immediate HTTP responses. Neither proves the advertised cross-process report-to-match flow.\n\nClosed #11 and #57 describe that outcome but do not currently deliver it.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Add containerized Firestore and Pub/Sub emulators (and a safe GCS-compatible local adapter/fake) to Compose.\n- Bootstrap canonical topics, subscriptions, collections, buckets, and test identities deterministically.\n- Configure every service through the same typed environment contract used in GCP.\n- Add health/readiness checks and dependency-aware startup without fixed sleeps.\n- Provide a fast deterministic AI profile for routine development/CI plus an opt-in real Ollama profile.\n- Provide one documented command to start, seed/reset, inspect logs, run the full report-to-match-to-notification smoke journey, and stop cleanly.\n- Add an emulator-backed automated test that crosses real process/HTTP/message boundaries and asserts durable side effects, not only response shapes.\n- Document emulator differences and any journey that still requires GCP.\n\nOfficial Pub/Sub emulator: https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/emulator\n\nOfficial Firestore emulator: https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/native/docs/emulator",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe matcher reads only hard-coded `lost-101`, injects Golden Retriever traits, and publishes a transient result without persisting it (`cmd/pet-matcher/worker.go:78-121`). The web API then seeds two fake matches whenever the match store is empty (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:480-556`). Unknown locations receive a Seattle fallback that can create a false proximity boost.\n\nClosed #61 added scoring helpers but not real candidate retrieval/indexing. Closed #90 added a match-store read but the producer never writes that store.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Query all eligible active lost reports within a bounded time/geographic candidate window.\n- Use persisted, image-derived traits for both lost and found reports; remove hard-coded candidate IDs and traits.\n- Reject or defer matching when required coordinates/images/traits are unavailable; never apply a default location.\n- Rank candidates deterministically and persist match records with stable idempotency keys before emitting notifications.\n- Store score components, distance, model/version, threshold version, timestamps, and explanation/provenance.\n- Exclude closed/reunited/expired reports in coordination with #94.\n- Remove automatic production match seeding; put demo fixtures behind an explicit development seed command.\n- Add multi-candidate, no-candidate, duplicate-event, model-failure, and threshold-boundary tests.\n- Validate precision/recall on a curated labeled image set before presenting an accuracy claim.\n\n## Dependencies\n\nDepends on #107, #108, the canonical schema issue, and #111.",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe forms collect meaningful product data, but the persisted events discard most of it.\n\n`LostPetFormRequest` includes name, species, breed, colors, description, phone, and email, while `LostPetEvent` retains only ID, email, time, and a location string. The found form similarly loses finder contact, species, breed, colors, custody, and extracted traits (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:127-136,285-300,342-350,428-443`; `pkg/domain/events.go:11-17,44-50`).\n\nThe current location is an unstructured string; unknown locations silently become Seattle center in `pkg/domain/geo.go:45-74`.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Define separate persisted aggregates, public DTOs, command requests, and versioned integration events.\n- Persist stable IDs, owner/finder identity references, timestamps, status, species/breed/colors/markings, description, custody, verified image object references, and validated coordinates.\n- Store private contact data separately from public listing data.\n- Represent geocoding status explicitly; never substitute a default coordinate for unknown input.\n- Define additive event evolution rules, schema version, stable event ID, and tolerant readers for in-flight messages.\n- Validate lengths, enums, timestamps, coordinates, and normalized contact data at the boundary.\n- Add migration/compatibility tests for every prior event shape already published by the app.\n- Update search and notification contracts to consume the canonical schema.\n\n## Related\n\nComplements #94 and is a prerequisite for real matching and notifications.",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe web frontend implements a second set of report APIs instead of using the report services:\n\n- Browser code posts to the web process (`cmd/web-frontend/static/js/lost-wizard.js:128-144`, `found-report.js:110-125`).\n- Web handlers save only to their private store and publish no events (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:206-308,352-451`).\n- The lost/found services use different collections and do publish events (`cmd/lostpet-service/service.go:63-75`, `cmd/foundpet-service/service.go:66-78`).\n\nA successful UI submission therefore bypasses the matcher cascade. Closed #90 connected handlers to an injected state interface but did not establish a shared or canonical application boundary.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Record the intended boundary: web as a BFF calling private report services, or shared application commands invoked by both HTTP adapters.\n- Keep one authoritative validation, persistence, event publication, error, and idempotency path per command.\n- Route browser submissions through that path and remove duplicate business logic.\n- Use explicit internal authentication for service-to-service calls in GCP.\n- Preserve public API compatibility or version any intentional contract change.\n- Return success only after the accepted durability/event-delivery guarantee is met.\n- Add contract tests that run the same cases through direct service and browser-facing entrypoints.\n- Add a full local journey proving a UI report reaches the matcher and match store.\n\n## Related\n\nDepends on #107 and #108; event reliability is tracked separately.",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nClosed #13 promised CI/CD, Workload Identity Federation, Artifact Registry, and deployment verification, but the repository has only `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. There is no `.dockerignore`.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Provision regional Artifact Registry repositories.\n- Authenticate GitHub to GCP with Workload Identity Federation; never store a service-account JSON key.\n- Add a `.dockerignore` excluding Git metadata, credentials, state, local provider caches, reports, and generated auth files.\n- Build each service once per commit, produce an SBOM and vulnerability result, and deploy the exact image digest.\n- Establish separate staging and production GitHub environments with appropriate approvals and scoped configuration.\n- Choose one deployment authority (OpenTofu or generated Cloud Run configuration) and remove manifest/IaC drift.\n- Run post-deploy health plus a real report-to-match smoke check in staging.\n- Promote the already-built digest to production and record the source SHA/digest.\n- Support tested Cloud Run traffic rollback without rebuilding.\n- Add concurrency controls so older deploys cannot overtake newer ones.\n\nArtifact Registry is the supported registry path: https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/transition/transition-from-gcr",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe matcher defaults to `http://localhost:11434` (`pkg/ollama/client.go:16,45-56`). OpenTofu provisions no inference service.\n\nThe local model currently resolves to a 7.2 GB multimodal Ollama artifact, while Cloud Run GPU workloads require an explicit GPU/resource, concurrency, quota, and cost design.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Record an ADR comparing private Cloud Run GPU/Ollama with an appropriate managed Vertex AI path.\n- Benchmark representative pet images for quality, p50/p95 latency, cold start, throughput, and per-report cost.\n- If retaining Ollama, provision a private authenticated inference service with supported GPU, CPU/memory, model loading, startup probe, timeout, concurrency, min/max instances, and quota.\n- Do not expose the inference API publicly.\n- Pin and record model artifact/version provenance with each match result.\n- Add bounded retries, circuit breaking, cancellation, and a user-visible deferred/retry state.\n- Keep the same inference contract locally and in GCP, with a fast deterministic fake for routine tests.\n- Document licensing, safety limitations, fallback behavior, and the operational runbook.\n\nCloud Run GPU requirements: https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/gpu\n\nOllama model inventory: https://ollama.com/library/gemma4",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nClosed #63 did not add authentication or sessions. All web routes are registered without auth middleware (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:47-71`). Any caller can confirm/reject a match, send a purported secure contact message, or mark a pet reunited (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:576-700`). Public lost-pet responses use the event model that contains `reporterEmail`.\n\nThis violates the repository rule that contact details and state-changing actions must not cross an unauthenticated or unauthorized boundary.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Integrate an OIDC provider or Google Identity Platform and validate sessions/tokens server-side.\n- Define user, reporter, finder, shelter/operator, and service identities and their permissions.\n- Store ownership on reports and matches; enforce it on every mutation and private read.\n- Return explicit redacted public DTOs that never expose reporter/finder contact details.\n- Implement secure mediated contact without revealing either party's details until policy allows it.\n- Add CSRF protection when cookie sessions are used and secure cookie/session rotation settings.\n- Return 401/403/404 consistently without leaking resource existence.\n- Record authorization-sensitive actions in an audit trail.\n- Add negative integration tests for anonymous, wrong-owner, expired-session, and privilege-escalation attempts.\n- Make #94 lifecycle mutations depend on this authorization boundary.\n\n## Related\n\nFollow-up to closed #63; notification-provider work remains tracked in #65.",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nEvery executable constructs its own in-memory state and event backend:\n\n- `cmd/lostpet-service/main.go:18-20`\n- `cmd/foundpet-service/main.go:19-22`\n- `cmd/pet-matcher/main.go:16-18`\n- `cmd/notification-service/main.go:14-15`\n- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:31-34`\n\nOnly memory implementations exist under `pkg/store`, `pkg/pubsub`, and `pkg/blob`; `go.mod` has no GCP client dependencies. State is process-local and disappears on restart, while an event published in one container cannot reach a subscriber in another. Collection names also disagree between the web frontend (`lost_pets`, `found_pets`) and services (`lostPets`, `foundPets`).\n\nClosed issues #3, #22, and #23 established interfaces and skeletal resources, but not a runnable managed-service path. Open #66 covers related infrastructure.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Implement Firestore, Cloud Pub/Sub, and GCS adapters using Application Default Credentials.\n- Add a typed runtime factory that selects explicit test, local-emulator, and GCP modes.\n- Reject memory adapters at production startup and fail fast on missing required configuration.\n- Define canonical collection, topic, subscription, and object-prefix names shared by all services.\n- Propagate cancellation and close/flush managed clients during shutdown.\n- Prove that one service can write/publish and another process can read/consume.\n- Prove state survives a service restart.\n- Add adapter contract tests and emulator-backed integration coverage.\n\n## Dependencies\n\nThis is foundational for #64, #65, #66, #91, and #94.",

    "body": "Surfaced by branch `test/docs-assertions` (#103). Two fail-open cases share one root cause: a guard reads only the first match, or only one line.\n\n**1. `TestLocalStackCommandMatchesCI` truncates at a continuation line.**\n`docker compose up --build --detach[^\\n]*` reads a single line. If **both** `ci.yml` and `AGENTS.md` reflow the command onto a continuation, a service dropped from one side is invisible. Reproduced: with both files reflowed and `web-frontend` dropped from CI, the suite reports `ok`.\n\nLatent today — both occurrences are single-line and that line has no wrapping pressure. The fix is to reuse the continuation-aware pattern already in the file: `(?:[^\\n]*\\\\\\n)*[^\\n]*`.\n\n**2. `markdownlintFiles` compares only the first invocation.**\nIt calls `FindString`, so a second `markdownlint-cli` block appended to either file is ignored. Three variants pass green: a duplicate block in `AGENTS.md` listing a bogus file; a second lint job in `ci.yml` listing a different file; and a second job pinned to a different `markdownlint-cli` version.\n\nThis is the only lookup in the file that ignores multiplicity — `ciStep` fatals on ambiguity, `versionPin.docs` checks every match, `assertCommandMatches` compares all occurrences. Behavior is also position-dependent: the same duplicate placed *earlier* fails loudly.\n\nFix: `FindAllString` and fatal when `len > 1`, matching `ciStep`'s ambiguity message.\n\n**3. Unquoted arguments are invisible.**\n`quotedArg` only extracts `\"...\"` tokens, so an unquoted `NEWDOC.md` added to the documented command is dropped from both the equality comparison and the existence check. Fix: fail if the invocation still contains an unquoted `\\S+\\.md` token after extraction.",

    "body": "## Problem\nPet reports are ingested as `LOST` or `FOUND`, but there are no HTTP endpoints or state machine handlers to update a pet's status to `REUNITED`, `EXPIRED`, or `CLOSED`.\n\n## Real-World Requirement\nPet owners and shelters need the ability to mark a lost pet as safely reunited or close a report. Updating status ensures resolved pets are excluded from active AI matching pipelines and live dashboards:\n- Define valid state transitions: `LOST` -> `REUNITED` / `EXPIRED`, `FOUND` -> `RESOLVED` / `EXPIRED`.\n- Add `PATCH /api/v1/lost-pets/{id}/status` and `PATCH /api/v1/found-pets/{id}/status` endpoints.\n- Emit `petStatusChanged` Pub/Sub events when status transitions occur.\n\n## Proposed Solution\n- Add `UpdateStatus` methods in `pkg/store`.\n- Expose `PATCH` handlers in `lostpet-service`, `foundpet-service`, and `web-frontend`.\n- Publish `petStatusChanged` events on Pub/Sub broker.\n\nRef: branch `main`",

    "body": "## Problem\n`cmd/pet-matcher` and `cmd/notification-service` event processing loops acknowledge or discard Pub/Sub messages immediately. If downstream dependencies (e.g. Ollama inference service, email gateway, Web Push endpoints) fail temporarily, messages are lost.\n\n## Real-World Requirement\nProduction event-driven microservices require message processing resilience:\n- Exponential backoff retry policies with configurable max attempt counters.\n- Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) forwarding for unprocessable (\"poison pill\") events after max retries.\n- Circuit breaker pattern for external HTTP/AI RPC calls.\n\n## Proposed Solution\n- Add retry and backoff wrapper in `pkg/pubsub`.\n- Implement DLQ topic forwarding (`lostPet-dlq`, `foundPet-dlq`, `matchFound-dlq`) when max retries are exceeded.\n\nRef: branch `main`",

    "body": "Surfaced by the workflow audit on `chore/pin-go-toolchain-and-harden-ci` (#47). Filed rather than fixed there, per `AGENTS.md` step 5 — it is a policy question, not a code defect.\n\n## Observation\n\nThe `main-protection` ruleset sets `required_approving_review_count: 0`. `AGENTS.md` step 11 explicitly allows self-merges, so this is intentional and consistent for a solo repository.\n\nThe consequence worth writing down: `code-review` is the only review in the chain, it is performed by an agent, and **CI cannot verify it ran**. If a sub-agent is unavailable, say so explicitly and state what you checked manually instead\"* — and that clause works in practice. Sessions where the harness cannot spawn subagents fall back to inline review with disclosure, which is the documented path.\n\nThe gap is that nothing records **which** commits got a real subagent review versus an inline one. After the fact, the two are indistinguishable in the history.\n\n## Options\n\n1. Do nothing. The disclosure convention is working; a solo repo may not need an audit trail.\n2. Require a trailer in the commit body — e.g. `Reviewed-by: code-review (subagent)` vs `Reviewed-by: inline (subagent unavailable)` — making the distinction greppable. Cheap, unenforceable, but honest.\n3. Set `required_approving_review_count: 1`. Strongest, but blocks solo work entirely and contradicts step 11 as written.\n\nOption 2 is the only one that adds signal without cost.     "body": "Surfaced by the workflow audit on `chore/pin-go-toolchain-and-harden-ci` (#47). Filed rather than fixed there, per `AGENTS.md` step 5 — out of scope for that slice.\n\n## Problem\n\n`static-checks` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` passes an explicit file list to markdownlint:\n\n```yaml\nnpx --yes markdownlint-cli@0.49.1 --config .markdownlint.json \\\n  \"AGENTS.md\" \"CLAUDE.md\" \"README.md\" \"docs/**/*.md\"\n```\n\n`docs/**/*.md` globs, but the three top-level files are enumerated by name. A new top-level Markdown file — say `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `SECURITY.md` — is silently unlinted, and the check still reports green.     "body": "Surfaced by the `verifier` sub-agent while auditing skip gates for #144.\n\n## Problem\n\n`GO_INTEGRATION_OLLAMA` gates `TestScoringPipeline_LiveOllamaIntegration` in\n`pkg/scoring/integration_test.go`. When the variable is unset the test calls\n`t.Skip` and the package still reports `ok` — identical in behaviour to the\nemulator-gated contracts.\n\nThe variable name appears in **no Markdown file in the repository**. Its sibling\n`PETSPOTR_GCS_INTEGRATION_BUCKET` is documented at `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:262`.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nThis is the same defect class #144 fixed for the emulator contracts: a silent\nskip that reads as coverage. AGENTS.md now warns that emulator-gated contracts\nskip silently and enumerates the packages, but that enumeration is about\nemulator host variables and does not cover this one. The CI section's \"do not\nclaim that coverage unless a task defines and runs an explicit integration\ncommand for it\" covers the risk in prose — an agent will not falsely claim live\nOllama coverage — but there is no way to discover how to actually *run* the\ntest, because the variable that enables it is undocumented.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\nDocument the variable in `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` next to\n`PETSPOTR_GCS_INTEGRATION_BUCKET`, with the command that runs the test and a\nnote about the model it requires. `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` owns integration\ncommands; per AGENTS.md they should not be copied into AGENTS.md itself.\n\nA follow-on worth considering: `docs/docs_test.go` is gaining guards that assert\nAGENTS.md's project table matches the tree. The same mechanism could assert that\nevery skip-gate environment variable in the tree is named in some Markdown file,\nwhich would have caught this one automatically.\n\nBranch that surfaced this: `docs/agents-md-accuracy-pass` (merged as #144).",

    "body": "Surfaced while implementing issue #108 on branch `feat/foundpet-pubsub-push`.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe repository verifies with Go 1.26.5, but `Dockerfile` still builds every service with `golang:1.22-alpine`. Google Cloud Pub/Sub v2 is the current client line, but its current release requires a newer Go toolchain than the container builder. The #108 slice therefore uses the compatible `cloud.google.com/go/pubsub` v1 client, which is deprecated upstream.\n\nThis does not block the authenticated push slice, but it leaves the production image toolchain behind CI and creates avoidable future migration debt.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Pin the Docker builder to the same Go 1.26.5 toolchain used by CI and `AGENTS.md`.\n- Migrate the managed publisher and emulator contract from `cloud.google.com/go/pubsub` v1 to `cloud.google.com/go/pubsub/v2`.\n- Preserve publish acknowledgement, topic reuse, client shutdown, emulator isolation, and redelivery integration coverage.\n- Rebuild every service image and run the full verifier and Playwright gates.\n- Update dependency and development documentation without changing the `go.mod` language version unless required and explicitly reviewed.\n\nReference: branch `feat/foundpet-pubsub-push`.",

    "body": "## Problem\n\nThe public web process exposes report creation, feature extraction/inference, upload signing, push subscription/test, contact, and lifecycle mutation endpoints with no rate limiting, quota enforcement, bot friction, or request-cost controls. Per-request body limits are useful but do not prevent repeated requests, storage exhaustion, notification abuse, or expensive model invocation.\n\nSurfaced during the repository readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:60-69` registers every API directly on the public mux.\n- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:267`, `:320`, `:413`, `:582`, `:632`, `:667`, and `:730` cap individual bodies but provide no caller- or route-level request budget.\n- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:308-340` performs feature extraction on submitted image data, an expensive path once real inference is connected.\n- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:626-652` and `:724-769` expose contact and push operations without delivery-abuse controls.\n- No rate-limiter, challenge, moderation queue, Cloud Armor policy, quota middleware, or abuse telemetry exists in `cmd/`, `pkg/`, or `infra/`.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Define a threat and cost model for anonymous report, upload, inference, contact, and notification operations.\n- Apply per-IP and, after authentication, per-account quotas with stricter route-specific limits for expensive or externally billable work.\n- Add bounded concurrency and queue/backpressure controls around inference and notification delivery.\n- Require single-use, short-lived upload intents and enforce storage/object quotas.\n- Add bot/spam defenses appropriate to the public reporting journey without blocking accessibility.\n- Record privacy-safe abuse metrics and alert on rejection rate, unusual spend, inference saturation, and notification spikes.\n- Define trusted-proxy/IP handling and test header spoofing before using client IP as an identity signal.\n- Add deterministic tests for burst, sustained, concurrent, and distributed-limit behavior.\n- Provision edge controls in code if the production ingress uses an external Application Load Balancer/Cloud Armor.\n\n## Scope\n\nThis complements #110 (identity/authorization), #109 (secure upload lifecycle), #111 (AI hosting), #121 (SLOs/alerts), and #122 (cost guardrails). Those issues do not define request-level abuse prevention.",

    "body": "## Problem\n\nThe match dashboard renders persisted match fields by interpolating them into an HTML string and assigning the result to `innerHTML`. Once real reports and persisted matcher output replace the current seed data, attacker-controlled pet names, breeds, locations, image URLs, or IDs can become stored DOM injection.\n\nSurfaced during the repository readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- `cmd/web-frontend/static/js/match-dashboard.js:41` assigns concatenated match-card markup to `container.innerHTML`.\n- `cmd/web-frontend/static/js/match-dashboard.js:45-139` interpolates `matchId`, pet name, breed, location, image URL, status, and score fields into HTML, attributes, and inline styles without contextual encoding.\n- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:555-572` returns persisted match documents directly to the browser.\n- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:47-71` registers the application without a response-security-header middleware; there is no Content Security Policy to reduce impact.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Construct match cards with DOM APIs and `textContent`, or apply proven contextual encoding for text and attribute values.\n- Validate image URLs against the application-owned storage policy before assigning them to `src`.\n- Treat match IDs and numeric score/style values as typed, validated data rather than markup.\n- Add a restrictive Content Security Policy and baseline response headers without relying on CSP as the primary injection fix.\n- Remove inline script/style dependencies needed to enforce the chosen CSP.\n- Add browser tests containing HTML, quote, and script-like payloads in every rendered persisted field and assert they remain inert.\n- Cover both server-seeded/test fixtures and the future canonical persisted-match path.\n\n## Scope\n\nThis issue is distinct from #110, which covers authentication, ownership, and contact privacy. It addresses browser-side output handling and defense in depth.",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nRepository and public-product claims have drifted from the code:\n\n- `docs/MIGRATION_PLAN.md` still describes Gemma 2, Dapr, and paths/topology that do not exist, and leaves referenced work unchecked even when issues are closed.\n- `docs/ROADMAP.md` treats closed issue status as product completion despite mock or in-process implementations.\n- `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` describes GCP deployment and multi-channel notifications as functional although runtime adapters/providers are absent.\n- The home page claims 98.4% AI accuracy, a sub-three-second cascade, 1,420+ reunions, and unconditional operational status (`cmd/web-frontend/templates/layout.html:58-80`) with no measurement source.\n- Success modals claim indexing and continuous matching even though the web handlers do not publish events.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Reconcile roadmap checkboxes with code evidence and current GitHub issue disposition.\n- Clearly distinguish demo, local-emulator, staging, and production capabilities.\n- Remove or qualify unsupported performance, accuracy, usage, reunion, and operational-status claims.\n- Make success UI reflect the actual durable workflow state (accepted, processing, matched, failed/retry).\n- Document the chosen canonical architecture, local profiles, cloud topology, configuration, deployment, and verification commands.\n- Add a prioritized dependency-ordered productization plan referencing #107 onward and existing #64/#65/#66/#91/#94.\n- Add a lightweight guard that detects stale linked issue state or document an explicit periodic review.\n- Update `AGENTS.md`'s docs inventory as tracked by #106 without duplicating that issue.\n\n## Related\n\nThis issue is documentation/product trust work; implementation remains in the linked feature issues.",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nKey interactions are mouse-only or lack accessible dialog behavior:\n\n- Upload drop zones are non-focusable `div` elements with hidden inputs and click/drop handlers only.\n- Navigation is hidden below 768px without a replacement.\n- Modals lack dialog semantics, focus trap/restore, and Escape handling.\n- Validation uses blocking `alert()` calls instead of field errors/live regions.\n- CSS has hover styling but no consistent `:focus-visible` or reduced-motion treatment.\n- Playwright defines no device projects or automated accessibility checks.\n\nClosed UI issues #50–#60 claimed WCAG/responsive coverage, but these behaviors remain.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Restore an operable mobile navigation pattern.\n- Use native file controls or make drop zones fully keyboard-operable with accessible names and announced status.\n- Add visible focus treatment and preserve logical tab order through the multi-step form.\n- Give modals correct dialog semantics, labels, focus trap/restore, Escape behavior, and background inertness.\n- Replace blocking alerts with field-associated errors and live regions.\n- Respect reduced motion and verify contrast in both themes.\n- Add automated accessibility checks and representative phone/tablet/desktop browser projects.\n- Complete the repository's manual `ui-review` gate with screenshots and keyboard evidence.\n\n## Related\n\nThis is a follow-up to the closed frontend milestone issues, not a replacement for real product data work.",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\n`status` is parsed but never applied (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:168-170,206-259,352-405`). Species is discarded on write and records without species pass a species filter. Pagination slices values collected from a Go map (`pkg/store/store.go:91-109`), whose iteration order is undefined, so page contents can duplicate or disappear between requests. Invalid query inputs silently fall back to defaults, and unknown locations silently become Seattle.\n\nClosed #93 claimed store-backed pagination and spatial filtering, but the implementation is in-memory, unstable, and only weakly tested.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Persist and enforce every documented filter.\n- Reject malformed limits, cursors, coordinates, radii, and incomplete geo parameter pairs with a clear 400 response.\n- Use a stable indexed sort with opaque cursor pagination; define tie-breaking behavior.\n- Guarantee adjacent pages cannot duplicate or omit records under a stable snapshot.\n- Treat missing/ungeocoded locations as unknown, never Seattle.\n- Return pagination metadata/links without exposing private fields.\n- Implement the same semantics in memory/emulator and Firestore adapters.\n- Add negative-filter, stable-order, insert-between-pages, boundary, and multi-page tests.\n\n## Related\n\nFollow-up to closed #61, #92, and #93; depends on #114 and Firestore indexes in #119.",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\n`cmd/pet-matcher/worker.go:60-69` passes `FoundPetEvent.ImageURL` directly in Ollama's `images` array. The Ollama API expects image data (base64 in the REST request), not an arbitrary application URL. Existing mock integration tests never validate the image payload, so this path can stay green without performing vision inference.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Resolve images only from trusted application storage using the verified object reference from #109/#114.\n- Enforce bounded size, supported MIME type, successful image decoding, and pixel/dimension limits before inference.\n- Encode image bytes in the format required by the configured Ollama API.\n- Do not allow arbitrary caller-controlled URLs or network fetches.\n- Classify corrupt image, missing object, transient inference, timeout, and invalid model-output failures.\n- Ensure logs/traces do not contain raw image bytes or signed URLs.\n- Add a payload-validating fake-Ollama integration test.\n- Add an opt-in real `gemma4:e2b` smoke test using a small licensed fixture.\n\nOfficial Ollama vision input guidance: https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/vision",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nCloud Run OpenTofu defines no concurrency, timeout, min/max instances, or resource policy (`infra/opentofu/modules/cloudrun/main.tf:1-54`). Worker manifests disable CPU throttling, and the proposed AI path can add GPU cost. No budget, forecast, anomaly, or quota alerts exist.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Load-test and set per-service CPU, memory, timeout, concurrency, min/max instances, and startup CPU settings.\n- Bound downstream pressure on Firestore, Pub/Sub, notification providers, and GPU quota.\n- Label resources for cost allocation and publish expected idle, normal, and peak monthly cost models.\n- Add actual-spend and forecast budget thresholds plus anomaly/quota notifications.\n- Define safe GPU scale-to-zero/min-instance behavior from #111 benchmarks.\n- Add a documented emergency cost-control response that preserves data integrity.\n- Revisit and record limits after staged load tests and production usage.\n\nCloud Run maximum instances: https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/max-instances\n\nCloud Billing budgets: https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nOpen #64 tracks instrumentation and probes, but the repository has no monitoring resources, service-level objectives, alert policies, uptime checks, notification channels, or runbooks. Existing JSON logger and pseudo-tracer are unused by service mains; no code records web request metrics, and `/healthz` always returns OK.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Complete #64's real structured logging, tracing, liveness, and dependency readiness first.\n- Define user-facing availability/latency and report-to-notification freshness SLOs.\n- Add alerts for Cloud Run 5xx/start failures, Pub/Sub backlog/oldest unacked/DLQ, Firestore errors, inference failures/latency, and notification delivery failure.\n- Add synthetic checks for the public entrypoint and a scheduled end-to-end staging canary.\n- Preserve correlation IDs across HTTP, outbox, Pub/Sub, matching, and notification boundaries.\n- Route alerts to an owned channel and link an actionable runbook from every policy.\n- Define PII-safe logging fields, sampling, and retention.\n- Test alert delivery and one incident/rollback exercise.\n\n## Related\n\nThis extends rather than duplicates #64.",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nRuntime configuration is scattered across implicit defaults for `PORT`, `OLLAMA_HOST`, and `OLLAMA_MODEL`. Cloud Run resources set no application environment or secret values. Notification workers use mock providers and hard-coded recipients/tokens. `.gitignore` permits a safe `.env.example`, but none exists.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Define centralized typed configuration per service with documented required, optional, default, and sensitive values.\n- Validate configuration before serving/consuming and fail production startup on missing bucket, project, collection, topic/subscription, endpoint, identity, or provider values.\n- Store session keys, notification credentials, VAPID material, and other secrets in Secret Manager.\n- Grant each runtime identity access only to its secrets and pin environment-secret versions deliberately.\n- Use ADC for Google APIs; do not mount or set service-account JSON credentials in Cloud Run.\n- Provide a non-secret `.env.example` and Compose defaults that work with emulators.\n- Document rotation, rollback, local overrides, and redaction rules.\n- Add tests for invalid modes, missing values, secret resolution, and log redaction.\n\n## Related\n\nProvider integration remains tracked in #65; service IAM remains part of #66.",

Neither proves the advertised cross-process report-to-match flow.\n\nClosed #11 and #57 describe that outcome but do not currently deliver it.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Add containerized Firestore and Pub/Sub emulators (and a safe GCS-compatible local adapter/fake) to Compose.\n- Bootstrap canonical topics, subscriptions, collections, buckets, and test identities deterministically.\n- Configure every service through the same typed environment contract used in GCP.\n- Add health/readiness checks and dependency-aware startup without fixed sleeps.\n- Provide a fast deterministic AI profile for routine development/CI plus an opt-in real Ollama profile.\n- Provide one documented command to start, seed/reset, inspect logs, run the full report-to-match-to-notification smoke journey, and stop cleanly.\n- Add an emulator-backed automated test that crosses real process/HTTP/message boundaries and asserts durable side effects, not only response shapes.\n- Document emulator differences and any journey that still requires GCP.\n\nOfficial Pub/Sub emulator: https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/emulator\n\nOfficial Firestore emulator: https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/native/docs/emulator",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe matcher reads only hard-coded `lost-101`, injects Golden Retriever traits, and publishes a transient result without persisting it (`cmd/pet-matcher/worker.go:78-121`).     "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe forms collect meaningful product data, but the persisted events discard most of it.\n\n`LostPetFormRequest` includes name, species, breed, colors, description, phone, and email, while `LostPetEvent` retains only ID, email, time, and a location string. The found form similarly loses finder contact, species, breed, colors, custody, and extracted traits (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:127-136,285-300,342-350,428-443`; `pkg/domain/events.go:11-17,44-50`).\n\nThe current location is an unstructured string; unknown locations silently become Seattle center in `pkg/domain/geo.go:45-74`.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Define separate persisted aggregates, public DTOs, command requests, and versioned integration events.\n- Persist stable IDs, owner/finder identity references, timestamps, status, species/breed/colors/markings, description, custody, verified image object references, and validated coordinates.\n- Store private contact data separately from public listing data.\n- Represent geocoding status explicitly; never substitute a default coordinate for unknown input.\n- Define additive event evolution rules, schema version, stable event ID, and tolerant readers for in-flight messages.\n- Validate lengths, enums, timestamps, coordinates, and normalized contact data at the boundary.\n- Add migration/compatibility tests for every prior event shape already published by the app.\n- Update search and notification contracts to consume the canonical schema.\n\n## Related\n\nComplements #94 and is a prerequisite for real matching and notifications.",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe web frontend implements a second set of report APIs instead of using the report services:\n\n- Browser code posts to the web process (`cmd/web-frontend/static/js/lost-wizard.js:128-144`, `found-report.js:110-125`).\n- Web handlers save only to their private store and publish no events (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:206-308,352-451`).\n- The lost/found services use different collections and do publish events (`cmd/lostpet-service/service.go:63-75`, `cmd/foundpet-service/service.go:66-78`).\n\nA successful UI submission therefore bypasses the matcher cascade. Closed #90 connected handlers to an injected state interface but did not establish a shared or canonical application boundary.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Record the intended boundary: web as a BFF calling private report services, or shared application commands invoked by both HTTP adapters.\n- Keep one authoritative validation, persistence, event publication, error, and idempotency path per command.\n- Route browser submissions through that path and remove duplicate business logic.\n- Use explicit internal authentication for service-to-service calls in GCP.\n- Preserve public API compatibility or version any intentional contract change.\n- Return success only after the accepted durability/event-delivery guarantee is met.\n- Add contract tests that run the same cases through direct service and browser-facing entrypoints.\n- Add a full local journey proving a UI report reaches the matcher and match store.\n\n## Related\n\nDepends on #107 and #108; event reliability is tracked separately.",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nClosed #13 promised CI/CD, Workload Identity Federation, Artifact Registry, and deployment verification, but the repository has only `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. There is no `.dockerignore`.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Provision regional Artifact Registry repositories.\n- Authenticate GitHub to GCP with Workload Identity Federation; never store a service-account JSON key.\n- Add a `.dockerignore` excluding Git metadata, credentials, state, local provider caches, reports, and generated auth files.\n- Build each service once per commit, produce an SBOM and vulnerability result, and deploy the exact image digest.\n- Establish separate staging and production GitHub environments with appropriate approvals and scoped configuration.\n- Choose one deployment authority (OpenTofu or generated Cloud Run configuration) and remove manifest/IaC drift.\n- Run post-deploy health plus a real report-to-match smoke check in staging.\n- Promote the already-built digest to production and record the source SHA/digest.\n- Support tested Cloud Run traffic rollback without rebuilding.\n- Add concurrency controls so older deploys cannot overtake newer ones.\n\nArtifact Registry is the supported registry path: https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/transition/transition-from-gcr",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe matcher defaults to `http://localhost:11434` (`pkg/ollama/client.go:16,45-56`). Its Cloud Run manifest has no `OLLAMA_HOST`, model-serving resource, authentication, or GPU and allocates only 2 CPU/2 GiB (`deploy/cloudrun/pet-matcher.yaml:9-18`). OpenTofu provisions no inference service.\n\nThe local model currently resolves to a 7.2 GB multimodal Ollama artifact, while Cloud Run GPU workloads require an explicit GPU/resource, concurrency, quota, and cost design.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Record an ADR comparing private Cloud Run GPU/Ollama with an appropriate managed Vertex AI path.\n- Benchmark representative pet images for quality, p50/p95 latency, cold start, throughput, and per-report cost.\n- If retaining Ollama, provision a private authenticated inference service with supported GPU, CPU/memory, model loading, startup probe, timeout, concurrency, min/max instances, and quota.\n- Do not expose the inference API publicly.\n- Pin and record model artifact/version provenance with each match result.\n- Add bounded retries, circuit breaking, cancellation, and a user-visible deferred/retry state.\n- Keep the same inference contract locally and in GCP, with a fast deterministic fake for routine tests.\n- Document licensing, safety limitations, fallback behavior, and the operational runbook.\n\nCloud Run GPU requirements: https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/gpu\n\nOllama model inventory: https://ollama.com/library/gemma4",

    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nClosed #63 did not add authentication or sessions. All web routes are registered without auth middleware (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:47-71`). Any caller can confirm/reject a match, send a purported secure contact message, or mark a pet reunited (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:576-700`). Public lost-pet responses use the event model that contains `reporterEmail`.\n\nThis violates the repository rule that contact details and state-changing actions must not cross an unauthenticated or unauthorized boundary.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Integrate an OIDC provider or Google Identity Platform and validate sessions/tokens server-side.\n- Define user, reporter, finder, shelter/operator, and service identities and their permissions.\n- Store ownership on reports and matches; enforce it on every mutation and private read.\n- Return explicit redacted public DTOs that never expose reporter/finder contact details.\n- Implement secure mediated contact without revealing either party's details until policy allows it.\n- Add CSRF protection when cookie sessions are used and secure cookie/session rotation settings.\n- Return 401/403/404 consistently without leaking resource existence.\n- Record authorization-sensitive actions in an audit trail.\n- Add negative integration tests for anonymous, wrong-owner, expired-session, and privilege-escalation attempts.\n- Make #94 lifecycle mutations depend on this authorization boundary.\n\n## Related\n\nFollow-up to closed #63; notification-provider work remains tracked in #65.",
