    "body": "Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n## Problem\n\nEvery executable constructs its own in-memory state and event backend:\n\n- `cmd/lostpet-service/main.go:18-20`\n- `cmd/foundpet-service/main.go:19-22`\n- `cmd/pet-matcher/main.go:16-18`\n- `cmd/notification-service/main.go:14-15`\n- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:31-34`\n\nOnly memory implementations exist under `pkg/store`, `pkg/pubsub`, and `pkg/blob`; `go.mod` has no GCP client dependencies. State is process-local and disappears on restart, while an event published in one container cannot reach a subscriber in another. Collection names also disagree between the web frontend (`lost_pets`, `found_pets`) and services (`lostPets`, `foundPets`).\n\nClosed issues #3, #22, and #23 established interfaces and skeletal resources, but not a runnable managed-service path. Open #66 covers related infrastructure.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Implement Firestore, Cloud Pub/Sub, and GCS adapters using Application Default Credentials.\n- Add a typed runtime factory that selects explicit test, local-emulator, and GCP modes.\n- Reject memory adapters at production startup and fail fast on missing required configuration.\n- Define canonical collection, topic, subscription, and object-prefix names shared by all services.\n- Propagate cancellation and close/flush managed clients during shutdown.\n- Prove that one service can write/publish and another process can read/consume.\n- Prove state survives a service restart.\n- Add adapter contract tests and emulator-backed integration coverage.\n\n## Dependencies\n\nThis is foundational for #64, #65, #66, #91, and #94.",

    "body": "Surfaced by branch `test/docs-assertions` (#103). Pre-existing on `main`, not introduced by that change.\n\n`TestRegisteredSubagentsDeferToAgentSourceOfTruth` iterates a hardcoded list:\n\n```go\nagentFiles := []string{\"ui-review.md\", \"verifier.md\", \"code-review.md\"}\n```\n\nA newly registered subagent is therefore unguarded. Confirmed: a `.claude/agents/planner.md` containing `go test -race`, `go1.26.5`, and `golangci-lint@v2.12.2 run`, with no mention of `AGENTS.md` at all, passes green.\n\nFix: read `.claude/agents/*.md` with `filepath.Glob`, fatal if the set is empty (so the guard fails closed if the directory moves), and iterate it. That tracks the registry rather than a snapshot of it.\n\nAlso minor, same test: the reference pattern `(^|[^\\w-])AGENTS\\.md($|[^\\w])` excludes `-` on the leading side to reject `NOT-AGENTS.md`, but the trailing group admits it, so `AGENTS.md-old` satisfies the guard. Should be `($|[^\\w-])`.",

    "body": "Surfaced by branch `test/docs-assertions` (#103). Two fail-open cases share one root cause: a guard reads only the first match, or only one line.\n\n**1. `TestLocalStackCommandMatchesCI` truncates at a continuation line.**\n`docker compose up --build --detach[^\\n]*` reads a single line. If **both** `ci.yml` and `AGENTS.md` reflow the command onto a continuation, a service dropped from one side is invisible. Reproduced: with both files reflowed and `web-frontend` dropped from CI, the suite reports `ok`.\n\nLatent today — both occurrences are single-line and that line has no wrapping pressure. The fix is to reuse the continuation-aware pattern already in the file: `(?:[^\\n]*\\\\\\n)*[^\\n]*`.\n\n**2. `markdownlintFiles` compares only the first invocation.**\nIt calls `FindString`, so a second `markdownlint-cli` block appended to either file is ignored. Three variants pass green: a duplicate block in `AGENTS.md` listing a bogus file; a second lint job in `ci.yml` listing a different file; and a second job pinned to a different `markdownlint-cli` version.\n\nThis is the only lookup in the file that ignores multiplicity — `ciStep` fatals on ambiguity, `versionPin.docs` checks every match, `assertCommandMatches` compares all occurrences. Behavior is also position-dependent: the same duplicate placed *earlier* fails loudly.\n\nFix: `FindAllString` and fatal when `len > 1`, matching `ciStep`'s ambiguity message.\n\n**3. Unquoted arguments are invisible.**\n`quotedArg` only extracts `\"...\"` tokens, so an unquoted `NEWDOC.md` added to the documented command is dropped from both the equality comparison and the existence check. Fix: fail if the invocation still contains an unquoted `\\S+\\.md` token after extraction.",

    "body": "## Problem\nPet reports are ingested as `LOST` or `FOUND`, but there are no HTTP endpoints or state machine handlers to update a pet's status to `REUNITED`, `EXPIRED`, or `CLOSED`.\n\n## Real-World Requirement\nPet owners and shelters need the ability to mark a lost pet as safely reunited or close a report. Updating status ensures resolved pets are excluded from active AI matching pipelines and live dashboards:\n- Define valid state transitions: `LOST` -> `REUNITED` / `EXPIRED`, `FOUND` -> `RESOLVED` / `EXPIRED`.\n- Add `PATCH /api/v1/lost-pets/{id}/status` and `PATCH /api/v1/found-pets/{id}/status` endpoints.\n- Emit `petStatusChanged` Pub/Sub events when status transitions occur.\n\n## Proposed Solution\n- Add `UpdateStatus` methods in `pkg/store`.\n- Expose `PATCH` handlers in `lostpet-service`, `foundpet-service`, and `web-frontend`.\n- Publish `petStatusChanged` events on Pub/Sub broker.\n\nRef: branch `main`",

    "body": "## Problem\n`cmd/pet-matcher` and `cmd/notification-service` event processing loops acknowledge or discard Pub/Sub messages immediately. If downstream dependencies (e.g. Ollama inference service, email gateway, Web Push endpoints) fail temporarily, messages are lost.\n\n## Real-World Requirement\nProduction event-driven microservices require message processing resilience:\n- Exponential backoff retry policies with configurable max attempt counters.\n- Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) forwarding for unprocessable (\"poison pill\") events after max retries.\n- Circuit breaker pattern for external HTTP/AI RPC calls.\n\n## Proposed Solution\n- Add retry and backoff wrapper in `pkg/pubsub`.\n- Implement DLQ topic forwarding (`lostPet-dlq`, `foundPet-dlq`, `matchFound-dlq`) when max retries are exceeded.\n\nRef: branch `main`",

    "body": "Surfaced by the workflow audit on `chore/pin-go-toolchain-and-harden-ci` (#47). Filed rather than fixed there, per `AGENTS.md` step 5 — it is a policy question, not a code defect.\n\n## Observation\n\nThe `main-protection` ruleset sets `required_approving_review_count: 0`. `AGENTS.md` step 11 explicitly allows self-merges, so this is intentional and consistent for a solo repository.\n\nThe consequence worth writing down: `code-review` is the only review in the chain, it is performed by an agent, and **CI cannot verify it ran**. Branch protection enforces four automated checks and squash-only merges; it has no way to know whether step 8 happened. The gate is honor-system by construction.\n\n`AGENTS.md` already anticipates the failure mode — *\"Never self-certify a gate. If a sub-agent is unavailable, say so explicitly and state what you checked manually instead\"* — and that clause works in practice. Sessions where the harness cannot spawn subagents fall back to inline review with disclosure, which is the documented path.\n\nThe gap is that nothing records **which** commits got a real subagent review versus an inline one. After the fact, the two are indistinguishable in the history.\n\n## Options\n\n1. Do nothing. The disclosure convention is working; a solo repo may not need an audit trail.\n2. Require a trailer in the commit body — e.g. `Reviewed-by: code-review (subagent)` vs `Reviewed-by: inline (subagent unavailable)` — making the distinction greppable. Cheap, unenforceable, but honest.\n3. Set `required_approving_review_count: 1`. Strongest, but blocks solo work entirely and contradicts step 11 as written.\n\nOption 2 is the only one that adds signal without cost. Option 1 is defensible.\n\n## Acceptance\n\nEither `AGENTS.md` gains an explicit statement that the review gate is unenforceable by CI and how the record is kept, or this issue is closed as intended-behavior with the reasoning captured in the thread.",

    "body": "Surfaced by the workflow audit on `chore/pin-go-toolchain-and-harden-ci` (#47). Filed rather than fixed there, per `AGENTS.md` step 5 — out of scope for that slice.\n\n## Problem\n\n`static-checks` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` passes an explicit file list to markdownlint:\n\n```yaml\nnpx --yes markdownlint-cli@0.49.1 --config .markdownlint.json \\\n  \"AGENTS.md\" \"CLAUDE.md\" \"README.md\" \"docs/**/*.md\"\n```\n\n`docs/**/*.md` globs, but the three top-level files are enumerated by name. A new top-level Markdown file — say `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `SECURITY.md` — is silently unlinted, and the check still reports green.     "body": "Surfaced by the `verifier` sub-agent while auditing skip gates for #144.\n\n## Problem\n\n`GO_INTEGRATION_OLLAMA` gates `TestScoringPipeline_LiveOllamaIntegration` in\n`pkg/scoring/integration_test.go`. When the variable is unset the test calls\n`t.Skip` and the package still reports `ok` — identical in behaviour to the\nemulator-gated contracts.\n\nThe variable name appears in **no Markdown file in the repository**. Its sibling\n`PETSPOTR_GCS_INTEGRATION_BUCKET` is documented at `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:262`.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nThis is the same defect class #144 fixed for the emulator contracts: a silent\nskip that reads as coverage. AGENTS.md now warns that emulator-gated contracts\nskip silently and enumerates the packages, but that enumeration is about\nemulator host variables and does not cover this one. The CI section's \"do not\nclaim that coverage unless a task defines and runs an explicit integration\ncommand for it\" covers the risk in prose — an agent will not falsely claim live\nOllama coverage — but there is no way to discover how to actually *run* the\ntest, because the variable that enables it is undocumented.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\nDocument the variable in `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` next to\n`PETSPOTR_GCS_INTEGRATION_BUCKET`, with the command that runs the test and a\nnote about the model it requires. `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` owns integration\ncommands; per AGENTS.md they should not be copied into AGENTS.md itself.\n\nA follow-on worth considering: `docs/docs_test.go` is gaining guards that assert\nAGENTS.md's project table matches the tree. The same mechanism could assert that\nevery skip-gate environment variable in the tree is named in some Markdown file,\nwhich would have caught this one automatically.\n\nBranch that surfaced this: `docs/agents-md-accuracy-pass` (merged as #144).",

Filed rather than fixed there, per `AGENTS.md` step 5 — out of scope for that slice.\n\n## Problem\n\n`static-checks` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` passes an explicit file list to markdownlint:\n\n```yaml\nnpx --yes markdownlint-cli@0.49.1 --config .markdownlint.json \\\n  \"AGENTS.md\" \"CLAUDE.md\" \"README.md\" \"docs/**/*.md\"\n```\n\n`docs/**/*.md` globs, but the three top-level files are enumerated by name. ===== #150 chore(ci): add native deployment artifact validation =====
Discovered while working on branch `test/product-code-only`.

Removing `deploy/deploy_test.go` eliminates brittle Go tests that inspect Docker, Compose, and Cloud Run files as text. The verifier confirmed existing product tests and OpenTofu native validation remain green, but the repository has no pinned native schema/configuration gate specifically for the Cloud Run manifests.

Add an appropriate native validation command and wire it into the verifier/CI workflow without reintroducing tests that parse repository files. Keep tool versions pinned and update AGENTS.md with the exact applicable command.

===== #146 docs(development): document GO_INTEGRATION_OLLAMA skip gate =====
Surfaced by the `verifier` sub-agent while auditing skip gates for #144.

## Problem

`GO_INTEGRATION_OLLAMA` gates `TestScoringPipeline_LiveOllamaIntegration` in
`pkg/scoring/integration_test.go`. When the variable is unset the test calls
`t.Skip` and the package still reports `ok` — identical in behaviour to the
emulator-gated contracts.

The variable name appears in **no Markdown file in the repository**. Its sibling
`PETSPOTR_GCS_INTEGRATION_BUCKET` is documented at `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:262`.

## Why it matters

This is the same defect class #144 fixed for the emulator contracts: a silent
skip that reads as coverage. AGENTS.md now warns that emulator-gated contracts
skip silently and enumerates the packages, but that enumeration is about
emulator host variables and does not cover this one. The CI section's "do not
claim that coverage unless a task defines and runs an explicit integration
command for it" covers the risk in prose — an agent will not falsely claim live
Ollama coverage — but there is no way to discover how to actually *run* the
test, because the variable that enables it is undocumented.

## Suggested fix

Document the variable in `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` next to
`PETSPOTR_GCS_INTEGRATION_BUCKET`, with the command that runs the test and a
note about the model it requires. `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` owns integration
commands; per AGENTS.md they should not be copied into AGENTS.md itself.

A follow-on worth considering: `docs/docs_test.go` is gaining guards that assert
AGENTS.md's project table matches the tree. The same mechanism could assert that
every skip-gate environment variable in the tree is named in some Markdown file,
which would have caught this one automatically.

Branch that surfaced this: `docs/agents-md-accuracy-pass` (merged as #144).

===== #141 refactor(outbox): share managed recovery loop =====
## Problem

`cmd/lostpet-service/main.go` and `cmd/foundpet-service/main.go` now duplicate the same managed outbox recovery lifecycle: bounded legacy-index backfill, one-minute completed-sweep cadence, five-second pending publication, cancellation, and logging. Future fixes can drift between the two producers.

## Suggested change

Extract a small shared recovery runner with injected topic, relay callback, backfiller, clock/cadence, and logger. Preserve the existing bounded batches, transactionally fenced relay semantics, and Cloud Run CPU/scaling requirements. Add focused lifecycle tests before replacing both entrypoint copies.

## Context

Surfaced on branch `feat/lostpet-notification-push` while completing #108. Kept out of that end-to-end delivery slice.

===== #132 chore(go): align container toolchain and migrate Pub/Sub v2 =====
Surfaced while implementing issue #108 on branch `feat/foundpet-pubsub-push`.

## Problem

The repository verifies with Go 1.26.5, but `Dockerfile` still builds every service with `golang:1.22-alpine`. Google Cloud Pub/Sub v2 is the current client line, but its current release requires a newer Go toolchain than the container builder. The #108 slice therefore uses the compatible `cloud.google.com/go/pubsub` v1 client, which is deprecated upstream.

This does not block the authenticated push slice, but it leaves the production image toolchain behind CI and creates avoidable future migration debt.

## Acceptance criteria

- Pin the Docker builder to the same Go 1.26.5 toolchain used by CI and `AGENTS.md`.
- Migrate the managed publisher and emulator contract from `cloud.google.com/go/pubsub` v1 to `cloud.google.com/go/pubsub/v2`.
- Preserve publish acknowledgement, topic reuse, client shutdown, emulator isolation, and redelivery integration coverage.
- Rebuild every service image and run the full verifier and Playwright gates.
- Update dependency and development documentation without changing the `go.mod` language version unless required and explicitly reviewed.

Reference: branch `feat/foundpet-pubsub-push`.

===== #129 feat(security): add abuse controls to public endpoints =====
## Problem

The public web process exposes report creation, feature extraction/inference, upload signing, push subscription/test, contact, and lifecycle mutation endpoints with no rate limiting, quota enforcement, bot friction, or request-cost controls. Per-request body limits are useful but do not prevent repeated requests, storage exhaustion, notification abuse, or expensive model invocation.

Surfaced during the repository readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Evidence

- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:60-69` registers every API directly on the public mux.
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:267`, `:320`, `:413`, `:582`, `:632`, `:667`, and `:730` cap individual bodies but provide no caller- or route-level request budget.
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:308-340` performs feature extraction on submitted image data, an expensive path once real inference is connected.
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:626-652` and `:724-769` expose contact and push operations without delivery-abuse controls.
- No rate-limiter, challenge, moderation queue, Cloud Armor policy, quota middleware, or abuse telemetry exists in `cmd/`, `pkg/`, or `infra/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define a threat and cost model for anonymous report, upload, inference, contact, and notification operations.
- Apply per-IP and, after authentication, per-account quotas with stricter route-specific limits for expensive or externally billable work.
- Add bounded concurrency and queue/backpressure controls around inference and notification delivery.
- Require single-use, short-lived upload intents and enforce storage/object quotas.
- Add bot/spam defenses appropriate to the public reporting journey without blocking accessibility.
- Record privacy-safe abuse metrics and alert on rejection rate, unusual spend, inference saturation, and notification spikes.
- Define trusted-proxy/IP handling and test header spoofing before using client IP as an identity signal.
- Add deterministic tests for burst, sustained, concurrent, and distributed-limit behavior.
- Provision edge controls in code if the production ingress uses an external Application Load Balancer/Cloud Armor.

## Scope

This complements #110 (identity/authorization), #109 (secure upload lifecycle), #111 (AI hosting), #121 (SLOs/alerts), and #122 (cost guardrails). Those issues do not define request-level abuse prevention.

===== #128 fix(frontend): prevent stored DOM injection in match rendering =====
## Problem

The match dashboard renders persisted match fields by interpolating them into an HTML string and assigning the result to `innerHTML`. Once real reports and persisted matcher output replace the current seed data, attacker-controlled pet names, breeds, locations, image URLs, or IDs can become stored DOM injection.

Surfaced during the repository readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Evidence

- `cmd/web-frontend/static/js/match-dashboard.js:41` assigns concatenated match-card markup to `container.innerHTML`.
- `cmd/web-frontend/static/js/match-dashboard.js:45-139` interpolates `matchId`, pet name, breed, location, image URL, status, and score fields into HTML, attributes, and inline styles without contextual encoding.
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:555-572` returns persisted match documents directly to the browser.
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:47-71` registers the application without a response-security-header middleware; there is no Content Security Policy to reduce impact.

## Acceptance criteria

- Construct match cards with DOM APIs and `textContent`, or apply proven contextual encoding for text and attribute values.
- Validate image URLs against the application-owned storage policy before assigning them to `src`.
- Treat match IDs and numeric score/style values as typed, validated data rather than markup.
- Add a restrictive Content Security Policy and baseline response headers without relying on CSP as the primary injection fix.
- Remove inline script/style dependencies needed to enforce the chosen CSP.
- Add browser tests containing HTML, quote, and script-like payloads in every rendered persisted field and assert they remain inert.
- Cover both server-seeded/test fixtures and the future canonical persisted-match path.

## Scope

This issue is distinct from #110, which covers authentication, ownership, and contact privacy. It addresses browser-side output handling and defense in depth.

===== #127 docs(roadmap): publish an evidence-based readiness plan =====
Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Problem

Repository and public-product claims have drifted from the code:

- `docs/MIGRATION_PLAN.md` still describes Gemma 2, Dapr, and paths/topology that do not exist, and leaves referenced work unchecked even when issues are closed.
- `docs/ROADMAP.md` treats closed issue status as product completion despite mock or in-process implementations.
- `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` describes GCP deployment and multi-channel notifications as functional although runtime adapters/providers are absent.
- The home page claims 98.4% AI accuracy, a sub-three-second cascade, 1,420+ reunions, and unconditional operational status (`cmd/web-frontend/templates/layout.html:58-80`) with no measurement source.
- Success modals claim indexing and continuous matching even though the web handlers do not publish events.

## Acceptance criteria

- Reconcile roadmap checkboxes with code evidence and current GitHub issue disposition.
- Clearly distinguish demo, local-emulator, staging, and production capabilities.
- Remove or qualify unsupported performance, accuracy, usage, reunion, and operational-status claims.
- Make success UI reflect the actual durable workflow state (accepted, processing, matched, failed/retry).
- Document the chosen canonical architecture, local profiles, cloud topology, configuration, deployment, and verification commands.
- Add a prioritized dependency-ordered productization plan referencing #107 onward and existing #64/#65/#66/#91/#94.
- Add a lightweight guard that detects stale linked issue state or document an explicit periodic review.
- Update `AGENTS.md`'s docs inventory as tracked by #106 without duplicating that issue.

## Related

This issue is documentation/product trust work; implementation remains in the linked feature issues.

===== #126 fix(frontend): make core journeys keyboard accessible =====
Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Problem

Key interactions are mouse-only or lack accessible dialog behavior:

- Upload drop zones are non-focusable `div` elements with hidden inputs and click/drop handlers only.
- Navigation is hidden below 768px without a replacement.
- Modals lack dialog semantics, focus trap/restore, and Escape handling.
- Validation uses blocking `alert()` calls instead of field errors/live regions.
- CSS has hover styling but no consistent `:focus-visible` or reduced-motion treatment.
- Playwright defines no device projects or automated accessibility checks.

Closed UI issues #50–#60 claimed WCAG/responsive coverage, but these behaviors remain.

## Acceptance criteria

- Restore an operable mobile navigation pattern.
- Use native file controls or make drop zones fully keyboard-operable with accessible names and announced status.
- Add visible focus treatment and preserve logical tab order through the multi-step form.
- Give modals correct dialog semantics, labels, focus trap/restore, Escape behavior, and background inertness.
- Replace blocking alerts with field-associated errors and live regions.
- Respect reduced motion and verify contrast in both themes.
- Add automated accessibility checks and representative phone/tablet/desktop browser projects.
- Complete the repository's manual `ui-review` gate with screenshots and keyboard evidence.

## Related

This is a follow-up to the closed frontend milestone issues, not a replacement for real product data work.

===== #125 fix(api): make filters and pagination deterministic =====
Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Problem

`status` is parsed but never applied (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:168-170,206-259,352-405`). Species is discarded on write and records without species pass a species filter. Pagination slices values collected from a Go map (`pkg/store/store.go:91-109`), whose iteration order is undefined, so page contents can duplicate or disappear between requests. Invalid query inputs silently fall back to defaults, and unknown locations silently become Seattle.

Closed #93 claimed store-backed pagination and spatial filtering, but the implementation is in-memory, unstable, and only weakly tested.

## Acceptance criteria

- Persist and enforce every documented filter.
- Reject malformed limits, cursors, coordinates, radii, and incomplete geo parameter pairs with a clear 400 response.
- Use a stable indexed sort with opaque cursor pagination; define tie-breaking behavior.
- Guarantee adjacent pages cannot duplicate or omit records under a stable snapshot.
- Treat missing/ungeocoded locations as unknown, never Seattle.
- Return pagination metadata/links without exposing private fields.
- Implement the same semantics in memory/emulator and Firestore adapters.
- Add negative-filter, stable-order, insert-between-pages, boundary, and multi-page tests.

## Related

Follow-up to closed #61, #92, and #93; depends on #114 and Firestore indexes in #119.

===== #124 feat(frontend): implement the linked public pet directory =====
Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Problem

Every navigation shell links to `/pets` (`cmd/web-frontend/templates/layout.html:22-27` and the report/match templates), but `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:47-72` registers no route. The root handler rejects any non-root path, so the primary “Pet Directory” navigation ends in 404.

Closed #55 and #60 describe a complete directory and browser journey, but the current code contains neither.

## Acceptance criteria

===== #94 feat(domain): implement pet status lifecycle state machine and status update HTTP endpoints =====
## Problem
Pet reports are ingested as `LOST` or `FOUND`, but there are no HTTP endpoints or state machine handlers to update a pet's status to `REUNITED`, `EXPIRED`, or `CLOSED`.

## Real-World Requirement
Pet owners and shelters need the ability to mark a lost pet as safely reunited or close a report. Updating status ensures resolved pets are excluded from active AI matching pipelines and live dashboards:
- Define valid state transitions: `LOST` -> `REUNITED` / `EXPIRED`, `FOUND` -> `RESOLVED` / `EXPIRED`.
- Add `PATCH /api/v1/lost-pets/{id}/status` and `PATCH /api/v1/found-pets/{id}/status` endpoints.
- Emit `petStatusChanged` Pub/Sub events when status transitions occur.

## Proposed Solution
- Add `UpdateStatus` methods in `pkg/store`.
- Expose `PATCH` handlers in `lostpet-service`, `foundpet-service`, and `web-frontend`.
- Publish `petStatusChanged` events on Pub/Sub broker.

Ref: branch `main`

===== #91 feat(pubsub): add exponential backoff retries and dead-letter queue (DLQ) handling to event workers =====
## Problem
`cmd/pet-matcher` and `cmd/notification-service` event processing loops acknowledge or discard Pub/Sub messages immediately. If downstream dependencies (e.g. Ollama inference service, email gateway, Web Push endpoints) fail temporarily, messages are lost.

## Real-World Requirement
Production event-driven microservices require message processing resilience:
- Exponential backoff retry policies with configurable max attempt counters.
- Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) forwarding for unprocessable ("poison pill") events after max retries.
- Circuit breaker pattern for external HTTP/AI RPC calls.

## Proposed Solution
- Add retry and backoff wrapper in `pkg/pubsub`.
- Implement DLQ topic forwarding (`lostPet-dlq`, `foundPet-dlq`, `matchFound-dlq`) when max retries are exceeded.

Ref: branch `main`

===== #129 feat(security): add abuse controls to public endpoints =====
## Problem

The public web process exposes report creation, feature extraction/inference, upload signing, push subscription/test, contact, and lifecycle mutation endpoints with no rate limiting, quota enforcement, bot friction, or request-cost controls. Per-request body limits are useful but do not prevent repeated requests, storage exhaustion, notification abuse, or expensive model invocation.

Surfaced during the repository readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Evidence

- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:60-69` registers every API directly on the public mux.
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:267`, `:320`, `:413`, `:582`, `:632`, `:667`, and `:730` cap individual bodies but provide no caller- or route-level request budget.
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:308-340` performs feature extraction on submitted image data, an expensive path once real inference is connected.
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:626-652` and `:724-769` expose contact and push operations without delivery-abuse controls.
- No rate-limiter, challenge, moderation queue, Cloud Armor policy, quota middleware, or abuse telemetry exists in `cmd/`, `pkg/`, or `infra/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define a threat and cost model for anonymous report, upload, inference, contact, and notification operations.
- Apply per-IP and, after authentication, per-account quotas with stricter route-specific limits for expensive or externally billable work.
- Add bounded concurrency and queue/backpressure controls around inference and notification delivery.

===== #128 fix(frontend): prevent stored DOM injection in match rendering =====
## Problem

The match dashboard renders persisted match fields by interpolating them into an HTML string and assigning the result to `innerHTML`. Surfaced during the repository readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Evidence

- `cmd/web-frontend/static/js/match-dashboard.js:41` assigns concatenated match-card markup to `container.innerHTML`.

- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:555-572` returns persisted match documents directly to the browser.
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:47-71` registers the application without a response-security-header middleware; there is no Content Security Policy to reduce impact.

## Acceptance criteria

- Construct match cards with DOM APIs and `textContent`, or apply proven contextual encoding for text and attribute values.
- Validate image URLs against the application-owned storage policy before assigning them to `src`.
- Treat match IDs and numeric score/style values as typed, validated data rather than markup.
- Add a restrictive Content Security Policy and baseline response headers without relying on CSP as the primary injection fix.
- Remove inline script/style dependencies needed to enforce the chosen CSP.
- Add browser tests containing HTML, quote, and script-like payloads in every rendered persisted field and assert they remain inert.
- Cover both server-seeded/test fixtures and the future canonical persisted-match path.

## Scope

This issue is distinct from #110, which covers authentication, ownership, and contact privacy. It addresses browser-side output handling and defense in depth.

===== #94 feat(domain): implement pet status lifecycle state machine and status update HTTP endpoints =====
## Problem
Pet reports are ingested as `LOST` or `FOUND`, but there are no HTTP endpoints or state machine handlers to update a pet's status to `REUNITED`, `EXPIRED`, or `CLOSED`.

## Real-World Requirement
Pet owners and shelters need the ability to mark a lost pet as safely reunited or close a report. Updating status ensures resolved pets are excluded from active AI matching pipelines and live dashboards:
- Define valid state transitions: `LOST` -> `REUNITED` / `EXPIRED`, `FOUND` -> `RESOLVED` / `EXPIRED`.
- Add `PATCH /api/v1/lost-pets/{id}/status` and `PATCH /api/v1/found-pets/{id}/status` endpoints.
- Emit `petStatusChanged` Pub/Sub events when status transitions occur.

## Proposed Solution
- Add `UpdateStatus` methods in `pkg/store`.
- Expose `PATCH` handlers in `lostpet-service`, `foundpet-service`, and `web-frontend`.
- Publish `petStatusChanged` events on Pub/Sub broker.

Ref: branch `main`

===== #91 feat(pubsub): add exponential backoff retries and dead-letter queue (DLQ) handling to event workers =====
## Problem
`cmd/pet-matcher` and `cmd/notification-service` event processing loops acknowledge or discard Pub/Sub messages immediately. If downstream dependencies (e.g. Ollama inference service, email gateway, Web Push endpoints) fail temporarily, messages are lost.

## Real-World Requirement
Production event-driven microservices require message processing resilience:
- Exponential backoff retry policies with configurable max attempt counters.
- Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) forwarding for unprocessable ("poison pill") events after max retries.
- Circuit breaker pattern for external HTTP/AI RPC calls.

## Proposed Solution
- Add retry and backoff wrapper in `pkg/pubsub`.
- Implement DLQ topic forwarding (`lostPet-dlq`, `foundPet-dlq`, `matchFound-dlq`) when max retries are exceeded.

Ref: branch `main`

===== #129 feat(security): add abuse controls to public endpoints =====
## Problem

The public web process exposes report creation, feature extraction/inference, upload signing, push subscription/test, contact, and lifecycle mutation endpoints with no rate limiting, quota enforcement, bot friction, or request-cost controls. Per-request body limits are useful but do not prevent repeated requests, storage exhaustion, notification abuse, or expensive model invocation.

Surfaced during the repository readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Evidence

- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:60-69` registers every API directly on the public mux.
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:267`, `:320`, `:413`, `:582`, `:632`, `:667`, and `:730` cap individual bodies but provide no caller- or route-level request budget.
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:308-340` performs feature extraction on submitted image data, an expensive path once real inference is connected.
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:626-652` and `:724-769` expose contact and push operations without delivery-abuse controls.
- No rate-limiter, challenge, moderation queue, Cloud Armor policy, quota middleware, or abuse telemetry exists in `cmd/`, `pkg/`, or `infra/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define a threat and cost model for anonymous report, upload, inference, contact, and notification operations.
- Apply per-IP and, after authentication, per-account quotas with stricter route-specific limits for expensive or externally billable work.
- Add bounded concurrency and queue/backpressure controls around inference and notification delivery.
- Require single-use, short-lived upload intents and enforce storage/object quotas.
- Add bot/spam defenses appropriate to the public reporting journey without blocking accessibility.
- Record privacy-safe abuse metrics and alert on rejection rate, unusual spend, inference saturation, and notification spikes.
- Define trusted-proxy/IP handling and test header spoofing before using client IP as an identity signal.
- Add deterministic tests for burst, sustained, concurrent, and distributed-limit behavior.
- Provision edge controls in code if the production ingress uses an external Application Load Balancer/Cloud Armor.

## Scope

This complements #110 (identity/authorization), #109 (secure upload lifecycle), #111 (AI hosting), #121 (SLOs/alerts), and #122 (cost guardrails). Those issues do not define request-level abuse prevention.

===== #128 fix(frontend): prevent stored DOM injection in match rendering =====
## Problem

The match dashboard renders persisted match fields by interpolating them into an HTML string and assigning the result to `innerHTML`. Once real reports and persisted matcher output replace the current seed data, attacker-controlled pet names, breeds, locations, image URLs, or IDs can become stored DOM injection.

Surfaced during the repository readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Evidence

- `cmd/web-frontend/static/js/match-dashboard.js:41` assigns concatenated match-card markup to `container.innerHTML`.
- `cmd/web-frontend/static/js/match-dashboard.js:45-139` interpolates `matchId`, pet name, breed, location, image URL, status, and score fields into HTML, attributes, and inline styles without contextual encoding.
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:555-572` returns persisted match documents directly to the browser.
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:47-71` registers the application without a response-security-header middleware; there is no Content Security Policy to reduce impact.

## Acceptance criteria

- Construct match cards with DOM APIs and `textContent`, or apply proven contextual encoding for text and attribute values.
- Validate image URLs against the application-owned storage policy before assigning them to `src`.
- Treat match IDs and numeric score/style values as typed, validated data rather than markup.
- Add a restrictive Content Security Policy and baseline response headers without relying on CSP as the primary injection fix.
- Remove inline script/style dependencies needed to enforce the chosen CSP.
- Add browser tests containing HTML, quote, and script-like payloads in every rendered persisted field and assert they remain inert.
- Cover both server-seeded/test fixtures and the future canonical persisted-match path.

## Scope

This issue is distinct from #110, which covers authentication, ownership, and contact privacy. It addresses browser-side output handling and defense in depth.

===== #94 feat(domain): implement pet status lifecycle state machine and status update HTTP endpoints =====
## Problem
Pet reports are ingested as `LOST` or `FOUND`, but there are no HTTP endpoints or state machine handlers to update a pet's status to `REUNITED`, `EXPIRED`, or `CLOSED`.

## Real-World Requirement
Pet owners and shelters need the ability to mark a lost pet as safely reunited or close a report. Updating status ensures resolved pets are excluded from active AI matching pipelines and live dashboards:
- Define valid state transitions: `LOST` -> `REUNITED` / `EXPIRED`, `FOUND` -> `RESOLVED` / `EXPIRED`.
- Add `PATCH /api/v1/lost-pets/{id}/status` and `PATCH /api/v1/found-pets/{id}/status` endpoints.
- Emit `petStatusChanged` Pub/Sub events when status transitions occur.

## Proposed Solution
- Add `UpdateStatus` methods in `pkg/store`.
- Expose `PATCH` handlers in `lostpet-service`, `foundpet-service`, and `web-frontend`.
- Publish `petStatusChanged` events on Pub/Sub broker.

Ref: branch `main`

===== #91 feat(pubsub): add exponential backoff retries and dead-letter queue (DLQ) handling to event workers =====
## Problem
`cmd/pet-matcher` and `cmd/notification-service` event processing loops acknowledge or discard Pub/Sub messages immediately. If downstream dependencies (e.g. Ollama inference service, email gateway, Web Push endpoints) fail temporarily, messages are lost.

## Real-World Requirement
Production event-driven microservices require message processing resilience:
- Exponential backoff retry policies with configurable max attempt counters.
- Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) forwarding for unprocessable ("poison pill") events after max retries.
- Circuit breaker pattern for external HTTP/AI RPC calls.

## Proposed Solution
- Add retry and backoff wrapper in `pkg/pubsub`.
- Implement DLQ topic forwarding (`lostPet-dlq`, `foundPet-dlq`, `matchFound-dlq`) when max retries are exceeded.

Ref: branch `main`

===== #128 fix(frontend): prevent stored DOM injection in match rendering =====
## Problem

The match dashboard renders persisted match fields by interpolating them into an HTML string and assigning the result to `innerHTML`. Once real reports and persisted matcher output replace the current seed data, attacker-controlled pet names, breeds, locations, image URLs, or IDs can become stored DOM injection.

Surfaced during the repository readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Evidence

- `cmd/web-frontend/static/js/match-dashboard.js:41` assigns concatenated match-card markup to `container.innerHTML`.
- `cmd/web-frontend/static/js/match-dashboard.js:45-139` interpolates `matchId`, pet name, breed, location, image URL, status, and score fields into HTML, attributes, and inline styles without contextual encoding.
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:555-572` returns persisted match documents directly to the browser.
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:47-71` registers the application without a response-security-header middleware; there is no Content Security Policy to reduce impact.

## Acceptance criteria

- Construct match cards with DOM APIs and `textContent`, or apply proven contextual encoding for text and attribute values.
- Validate image URLs against the application-owned storage policy before assigning them to `src`.
- Treat match IDs and numeric score/style values as typed, validated data rather than markup.
- Add a restrictive Content Security Policy and baseline response headers without relying on CSP as the primary injection fix.
- Remove inline script/style dependencies needed to enforce the chosen CSP.
- Add browser tests containing HTML, quote, and script-like payloads in every rendered persisted field and assert they remain inert.
- Cover both server-seeded/test fixtures and the future canonical persisted-match path.

## Scope

This issue is distinct from #110, which covers authentication, ownership, and contact privacy. It addresses browser-side output handling and defense in depth.

- Document state recovery and lock/concurrency procedures.

Google Terraform security practices: https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/terraform/best-practices/security

===== #117 feat(local): run the full cascade against shared emulators =====
Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Problem

`docker compose up --build` starts isolated service containers plus Ollama, but no shared state or event transport (`docker-compose.yml:28-84`). The Go cascade tests share one in-process memory broker; Playwright starts only lost, found, and web services and checks immediate HTTP responses. Neither proves the advertised cross-process report-to-match flow.

Closed #11 and #57 describe that outcome but do not currently deliver it.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add containerized Firestore and Pub/Sub emulators (and a safe GCS-compatible local adapter/fake) to Compose.
- Bootstrap canonical topics, subscriptions, collections, buckets, and test identities deterministically.
- Configure every service through the same typed environment contract used in GCP.
- Add health/readiness checks and dependency-aware startup without fixed sleeps.
- Provide a fast deterministic AI profile for routine development/CI plus an opt-in real Ollama profile.
- Provide one documented command to start, seed/reset, inspect logs, run the full report-to-match-to-notification smoke journey, and stop cleanly.
- Add an emulator-backed automated test that crosses real process/HTTP/message boundaries and asserts durable side effects, not only response shapes.
- Document emulator differences and any journey that still requires GCP.

Official Pub/Sub emulator: https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/emulator

Official Firestore emulator: https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/native/docs/emulator

===== #115 feat(matcher): score active candidates and persist real matches =====
Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Problem

The matcher reads only hard-coded `lost-101`, injects Golden Retriever traits, and publishes a transient result without persisting it (`cmd/pet-matcher/worker.go:78-121`). The web API then seeds two fake matches whenever the match store is empty (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:480-556`). Unknown locations receive a Seattle fallback that can create a false proximity boost.

Closed #61 added scoring helpers but not real candidate retrieval/indexing. Closed #90 added a match-store read but the producer never writes that store.

## Acceptance criteria

- Query all eligible active lost reports within a bounded time/geographic candidate window.
- Use persisted, image-derived traits for both lost and found reports; remove hard-coded candidate IDs and traits.
- Reject or defer matching when required coordinates/images/traits are unavailable; never apply a default location.
- Rank candidates deterministically and persist match records with stable idempotency keys before emitting notifications.
- Store score components, distance, model/version, threshold version, timestamps, and explanation/provenance.
- Exclude closed/reunited/expired reports in coordination with #94.
- Remove automatic production match seeding; put demo fixtures behind an explicit development seed command.
- Add multi-candidate, no-candidate, duplicate-event, model-failure, and threshold-boundary tests.
- Validate precision/recall on a curated labeled image set before presenting an accuracy claim.

## Dependencies

Depends on #107, #108, the canonical schema issue, and #111.

===== #114 feat(domain): define complete versioned report schemas =====
Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Problem

The forms collect meaningful product data, but the persisted events discard most of it.

`LostPetFormRequest` includes name, species, breed, colors, description, phone, and email, while `LostPetEvent` retains only ID, email, time, and a location string. The found form similarly loses finder contact, species, breed, colors, custody, and extracted traits (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:127-136,285-300,342-350,428-443`; `pkg/domain/events.go:11-17,44-50`).

The current location is an unstructured string; unknown locations silently become Seattle center in `pkg/domain/geo.go:45-74`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define separate persisted aggregates, public DTOs, command requests, and versioned integration events.
- Persist stable IDs, owner/finder identity references, timestamps, status, species/breed/colors/markings, description, custody, verified image object references, and validated coordinates.
- Store private contact data separately from public listing data.
- Represent geocoding status explicitly; never substitute a default coordinate for unknown input.
- Define additive event evolution rules, schema version, stable event ID, and tolerant readers for in-flight messages.
- Validate lengths, enums, timestamps, coordinates, and normalized contact data at the boundary.
- Add migration/compatibility tests for every prior event shape already published by the app.
- Update search and notification contracts to consume the canonical schema.

## Related

Complements #94 and is a prerequisite for real matching and notifications.

===== #113 refactor(api): route web workflows through canonical services =====
Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Problem

The web frontend implements a second set of report APIs instead of using the report services:

- Browser code posts to the web process (`cmd/web-frontend/static/js/lost-wizard.js:128-144`, `found-report.js:110-125`).
- Web handlers save only to their private store and publish no events (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:206-308,352-451`).
- The lost/found services use different collections and do publish events (`cmd/lostpet-service/service.go:63-75`, `cmd/foundpet-service/service.go:66-78`).

A successful UI submission therefore bypasses the matcher cascade. Closed #90 connected handlers to an injected state interface but did not establish a shared or canonical application boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- Record the intended boundary: web as a BFF calling private report services, or shared application commands invoked by both HTTP adapters.
- Keep one authoritative validation, persistence, event publication, error, and idempotency path per command.
- Route browser submissions through that path and remove duplicate business logic.
- Use explicit internal authentication for service-to-service calls in GCP.
- Preserve public API compatibility or version any intentional contract change.
- Return success only after the accepted durability/event-delivery guarantee is met.
- Add contract tests that run the same cases through direct service and browser-facing entrypoints.
- Add a full local journey proving a UI report reaches the matcher and match store.

## Related

Depends on #107 and #108; event reliability is tracked separately.

===== #112 chore(cd): deploy immutable revisions through staged environments =====
Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Problem

Closed #13 promised CI/CD, Workload Identity Federation, Artifact Registry, and deployment verification, but the repository has only `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. All OpenTofu variables and Cloud Run manifests use mutable `gcr.io/petspotr/*:latest`; `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` assumes images already exist and deploys manually. There is no `.dockerignore`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Provision regional Artifact Registry repositories.
- Authenticate GitHub to GCP with Workload Identity Federation; never store a service-account JSON key.
- Add a `.dockerignore` excluding Git metadata, credentials, state, local provider caches, reports, and generated auth files.
- Build each service once per commit, produce an SBOM and vulnerability result, and deploy the exact image digest.
- Establish separate staging and production GitHub environments with appropriate approvals and scoped configuration.
- Choose one deployment authority (OpenTofu or generated Cloud Run configuration) and remove manifest/IaC drift.
- Run post-deploy health plus a real report-to-match smoke check in staging.
- Promote the already-built digest to production and record the source SHA/digest.
- Support tested Cloud Run traffic rollback without rebuilding.
- Add concurrency controls so older deploys cannot overtake newer ones.

Artifact Registry is the supported registry path: https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/transition/transition-from-gcr

===== #111 feat(ai): provision private Gemma 4 inference on GCP =====
Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Problem

The matcher defaults to `http://localhost:11434` (`pkg/ollama/client.go:16,45-56`). Its Cloud Run manifest has no `OLLAMA_HOST`, model-serving resource, authentication, or GPU and allocates only 2 CPU/2 GiB (`deploy/cloudrun/pet-matcher.yaml:9-18`). OpenTofu provisions no inference service.

The local model currently resolves to a 7.2 GB multimodal Ollama artifact, while Cloud Run GPU workloads require an explicit GPU/resource, concurrency, quota, and cost design.

## Acceptance criteria

- Record an ADR comparing private Cloud Run GPU/Ollama with an appropriate managed Vertex AI path.
- Benchmark representative pet images for quality, p50/p95 latency, cold start, throughput, and per-report cost.
- If retaining Ollama, provision a private authenticated inference service with supported GPU, CPU/memory, model loading, startup probe, timeout, concurrency, min/max instances, and quota.
- Do not expose the inference API publicly.
- Pin and record model artifact/version provenance with each match result.
- Add bounded retries, circuit breaking, cancellation, and a user-visible deferred/retry state.
- Keep the same inference contract locally and in GCP, with a fast deterministic fake for routine tests.
- Document licensing, safety limitations, fallback behavior, and the operational runbook.

Cloud Run GPU requirements: https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/gpu

Ollama model inventory: https://ollama.com/library/gemma4

===== #110 feat(auth): enforce identity ownership and contact privacy =====
Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Problem

Closed #63 did not add authentication or sessions. All web routes are registered without auth middleware (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:47-71`). Any caller can confirm/reject a match, send a purported secure contact message, or mark a pet reunited (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:576-700`). Public lost-pet responses use the event model that contains `reporterEmail`.

This violates the repository rule that contact details and state-changing actions must not cross an unauthenticated or unauthorized boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- Integrate an OIDC provider or Google Identity Platform and validate sessions/tokens server-side.
- Define user, reporter, finder, shelter/operator, and service identities and their permissions.
- Store ownership on reports and matches; enforce it on every mutation and private read.
- Return explicit redacted public DTOs that never expose reporter/finder contact details.
- Implement secure mediated contact without revealing either party's details until policy allows it.
- Add CSRF protection when cookie sessions are used and secure cookie/session rotation settings.
- Return 401/403/404 consistently without leaking resource existence.
- Record authorization-sensitive actions in an audit trail.
- Add negative integration tests for anonymous, wrong-owner, expired-session, and privilege-escalation attempts.
- Make #94 lifecycle mutations depend on this authorization boundary.

## Related

Follow-up to closed #63; notification-provider work remains tracked in #65.

===== #107 feat(runtime): implement durable managed-service adapters =====
Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.

## Problem

Every executable constructs its own in-memory state and event backend:

- `cmd/lostpet-service/main.go:18-20`
- `cmd/foundpet-service/main.go:19-22`
- `cmd/pet-matcher/main.go:16-18`
- `cmd/notification-service/main.go:14-15`
- `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:31-34`

Only memory implementations exist under `pkg/store`, `pkg/pubsub`, and `pkg/blob`; `go.mod` has no GCP client dependencies. State is process-local and disappears on restart, while an event published in one container cannot reach a subscriber in another. Collection names also disagree between the web frontend (`lost_pets`, `found_pets`) and services (`lostPets`, `foundPets`).

Closed issues #3, #22, and #23 established interfaces and skeletal resources, but not a runnable managed-service path. Open #66 covers related infrastructure.

## Acceptance criteria

- Implement Firestore, Cloud Pub/Sub, and GCS adapters using Application Default Credentials.
- Add a typed runtime factory that selects explicit test, local-emulator, and GCP modes.
- Reject memory adapters at production startup and fail fast on missing required configuration.
- Define canonical collection, topic, subscription, and object-prefix names shared by all services.
- Propagate cancellation and close/flush managed clients during shutdown.
- Prove that one service can write/publish and another process can read/consume.
- Prove state survives a service restart.
- Add adapter contract tests and emulator-backed integration coverage.

## Dependencies

This is foundational for #64, #65, #66, #91, and #94.

===== #94 feat(domain): implement pet status lifecycle state machine and status update HTTP endpoints =====
## Problem
Pet reports are ingested as `LOST` or `FOUND`, but there are no HTTP endpoints or state machine handlers to update a pet's status to `REUNITED`, `EXPIRED`, or `CLOSED`.

## Real-World Requirement
Pet owners and shelters need the ability to mark a lost pet as safely reunited or close a report. Updating status ensures resolved pets are excluded from active AI matching pipelines and live dashboards:
- Define valid state transitions: `LOST` -> `REUNITED` / `EXPIRED`, `FOUND` -> `RESOLVED` / `EXPIRED`.
- Add `PATCH /api/v1/lost-pets/{id}/status` and `PATCH /api/v1/found-pets/{id}/status` endpoints.
- Emit `petStatusChanged` Pub/Sub events when status transitions occur.

## Proposed Solution
- Add `UpdateStatus` methods in `pkg/store`.
- Expose `PATCH` handlers in `lostpet-service`, `foundpet-service`, and `web-frontend`.
- Publish `petStatusChanged` events on Pub/Sub broker.

Ref: branch `main`

===== #91 feat(pubsub): add exponential backoff retries and dead-letter queue (DLQ) handling to event workers =====
## Problem
`cmd/pet-matcher` and `cmd/notification-service` event processing loops acknowledge or discard Pub/Sub messages immediately. If downstream dependencies (e.g. Ollama inference service, email gateway, Web Push endpoints) fail temporarily, messages are lost.

## Real-World Requirement
Production event-driven microservices require message processing resilience:
- Exponential backoff retry policies with configurable max attempt counters.
- Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) forwarding for unprocessable ("poison pill") events after max retries.
- Circuit breaker pattern for external HTTP/AI RPC calls.

## Proposed Solution
- Add retry and backoff wrapper in `pkg/pubsub`.
- Implement DLQ topic forwarding (`lostPet-dlq`, `foundPet-dlq`, `matchFound-dlq`) when max retries are exceeded.

Ref: branch `main`

===== #66 feat(infra): update OpenTofu configuration for Go Web frontend Cloud Run deployment =====
## Description
Update OpenTofu infrastructure modules (`infra/opentofu`) and Cloud Run deployment manifests (`deploy/cloudrun`) to support provisioning, building, and deploying the modern Web Frontend service.

- Add Cloud Run module configuration for `web-frontend` service in OpenTofu.

Enhance `cmd/notification-service` to support production notification providers including SendGrid/SMTP for emails, Twilio for SMS alerts, and Web Push notifications, replacing log-only output.

## Acceptance Criteria

===== #64 feat(api): implement OpenTelemetry tracing, structured logging, and health/readiness probes =====
## Description
Prepare PetSpotR backend services for production operation by adding standardized `/healthz` (liveness) and `/readyz` (readiness) HTTP probes, structured JSON logging with correlation IDs, and OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed trace collection.

## Recommendation

Pick up [#128: prevent stored DOM injection in match rendering](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/128) next, split into two ordered slices.

The first slice should be:

`fix(frontend): render persisted matches safely`

- Replace the match-card `innerHTML` construction with DOM APIs and `textContent`. The current sink directly interpolates persisted IDs, names, locations, breeds, URLs, and scores into markup: [match-dashboard.js](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/petspotr/cmd/web-frontend/static/js/match-dashboard.js:41).
- Validate and restrict image sources before assigning `src`.
- Coerce and bound IDs, dates, statuses, and numeric score values.
- Add browser coverage with hostile HTML, quote, URL, and script-like field values, asserting they remain inert.
- Complete the required UI review, verifier, and code-review gates.
- Open the PR as `Part of #128`.

A second slice should externalize inline handlers/styles and add the restrictive CSP and baseline response headers needed to close #128. Keeping that separate prevents a security fix from turning into a repository-wide styling rewrite.

Why this is next:

- `main` is clean and exactly synchronized with protected remote `main` at `7a7d990`; there are currently no open PRs.
- The finding remains present in current code, while the API returns stored match records directly: [server.go](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/petspotr/cmd/web-frontend/server.go:597).
- It has no architectural or external-service dependency.
- It becomes directly exposed once [#115](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/115) starts persisting real, user-derived match data, so fixing it first avoids building new product behavior on an unsafe renderer.

After #128, I would follow this product sequence:

1. [#114](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/114) — canonical, versioned report schemas.
2. [#113](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/113) — route browser reports through the canonical services.
3. [#115](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/115) — match real candidates and persist real matches.
4. [#110](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/110) — identity and ownership, after selecting an identity provider and splitting the large issue into reviewable slices.

I would not prioritize the small CI/docs chores such as [#150](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/150) or #146 ahead of product and security work.

The issue tracker also needs reconciliation: #123 appears delivered by PR #143; #104/#105 refer to repository-inspection tests removed by PR #151; #106/#127 reference planning documents removed by PR #149; and #107/#66 are substantially implemented. Those should be closed or narrowed, but not via a separate development PR.

One operational note: the configured `gh` credential is invalid. Public read-only triage worked, but authentication must be refreshed before issue updates, pushing, or opening a PR.

No files were changed and no test suites were run during this triage.

---
name: fix-finding
description: Use when the user explicitly asks to fix and verify a validated or plausible security finding. Do not use as the primary trigger for full PR, commit, branch, patch, or repository scans.
---

# Fix Finding

## Objective

Turn a current security finding into a minimal, validated code change. If the code is already safe, prove that and report that no change was needed.

Judge the result in this order:

1. the current state is correctly classified as vulnerable, already safe, or unproven
2. any fix completely closes the broken security boundary
3. legitimate behavior and compatibility are preserved
4. relevant repository checks pass
5. the implementation follows repository conventions
6. the patch contains only the scope necessary for the earlier properties

Never trade an earlier property for a later one. Minimal means the smallest repository-native change that satisfies all earlier properties, not the fewest lines.

## Patch Contract

Before editing, establish from repository evidence:

- affected component and current source-to-sink path or broken control
- attacker-controlled input and required preconditions
- security invariant and narrowest plausible enforcement boundary
- legitimate behavior, APIs, error semantics, and compatibility constraints to preserve or intentionally change with supporting product evidence
- available PoC, reproducer, tests, evidence, and affected locations
- nearest relevant helpers and implementation, error-handling, and test precedents

Inspect the repository to fill gaps. Ask the user only when a material product, security, or compatibility decision remains.

## Runtime Validation

Use this guidance whenever reproducing the finding, running tests, or validating the fix:

- Complete the patch contract before broad setup; start with the smallest high-signal check through the real vulnerable boundary.
- Use repository-supported setup commands. Keep repair effort bounded so it does not displace path analysis, patching, or focused verification.
- Do not stop a progressing command merely because it is slow. Inspect process state, logs, artifacts, or resource use first.
- If runtime validation remains unavailable, use the strongest targeted static or harness-based artifact that preserves the real integration boundary. Do not substitute a simplified harness that removes the behavior being protected. Record every unrun check as unknown.

## Workflow

1. Revalidate and scope the finding.
   - Inspect repository instructions, affected code, direct callers, and only the context needed to prove the vulnerable path.
   - Establish concrete reachability in the current checkout; generic weakness labels, file anchors, and suspicious-looking code are not proof.
   - If the same broken security boundary cannot be shown after a bounded investigation, do not patch an adjacent weakness or add speculative defense in depth. Return `no_change` when evidence shows the path is already safe; otherwise return `blocked` with the missing proof.
   - Complete the patch contract and inspect relevant helpers, controls, and implementation and test precedents.
2. Reproduce or encode the issue before fixing when feasible.
   - Prefer a failing regression test, unit test, integration test, property test, or realistic-interface reproduction.
   - Capture the malicious condition and at least one legitimate control through the same boundary before implementation.
   - Keep an unsafe-behavior test only when it is safe, deterministic, and appropriate for the repository. Otherwise use the strongest repeatable validation artifact available and record the gap.
   - If the issue no longer reproduces before any code changes, investigate whether it was already fixed and preserve the validation evidence.
3. Choose the patch strategy.
   - Determine whether a narrow tactical change can close the boundary while preserving the patch contract.
   - Consider broader remediation only when the narrow option cannot close the boundary without breaking supported behavior. Remove or disable functionality only when repository or product evidence supports that mitigation.
   - If the only complete fix requires an unresolved decision about product policy, public-API compatibility, or cross-subsystem ownership, return `blocked` with the options, security tradeoff, and likely owner or codeowner when available.
   - Use nearby variants to test the chosen boundary. Report unrelated sibling findings or longer-term architectural work separately instead of expanding this patch.
4. Implement the fix and its proof.
   - Make the smallest repository-native change that fully enforces the invariant.
   - Prefer existing helpers and abstractions. Preserve APIs, legitimate inputs, and error semantics unless changing them is required by the security contract.
   - Handle unsafe state explicitly; do not silently accept, truncate, or reinterpret it.
   - Avoid unrelated refactors and preserve user changes outside the candidate patch.
   - Add focused regression coverage that fails on the vulnerable behavior and passes after the fix.
   - Include positive coverage for the legitimate control. Test at the lowest level that proves the invariant and through the realistic interface when feasible.
5. Verify in order.
   - **Applicability and buildability**: inspect the final diff for unrelated changes, then run the narrowest relevant syntax, import, build, type, or focused test check.
   - **Security closure**: rerun the original PoC, trigger, or strongest exploit check. Re-trace the source-to-sink or broken-control path in the patched code.
   - **Change-aware bypass review**: reread the finding and final diff without relying on the original rationale. Trace changed branches from direct callers, check equivalent sinks, and exercise an alternate malicious input class when practical.
   - **Preserved behavior**: rerun the legitimate control and confirm the recorded APIs, error semantics, and compatibility constraints remain intact.
   - **Repository checks**: run the focused regression tests, the owning package's relevant tests, and applicable formatter, linter, type checker, dependency, and integration checks.
   - Confirm the regression check would fail if the security change were removed, when practical.
   - Treat a failed earlier gate as disqualifying. Revise only the candidate changes or return `blocked`; never compensate for failed security closure or behavior preservation with style, smaller scope, or additional reporting.
6. Report the outcome with exact commands, results, changed files, and remaining risk.

## Workbench Remediation Stages

When a Codex Security workbench request includes a scan ID, occurrence ID, remediation request ID, action token, and expected version, follow only the requested remediation stage. The stage boundary changes when code may be written, but it does not weaken the validation requirements above.

- **Generate**: Keep the selected target checkout unchanged. Use an isolated worktree or temporary copy when edits are needed to develop or test the fix. Apply the patch contract and strategy gates above, write one canonical unified diff containing the complete source and regression-test change, then record `generated` or `failed` using the supplied workbench identity.
- **Apply**: Verify the recorded base revision and patch digest, then apply exactly that patch to the selected working tree without unrelated edits. Record `applied` or `failed`. Do not verify or close the finding in this stage.
- **Verify**: Do not modify source. Run the ordered verification gates above against the recorded patch. Record `verified` only when the original issue no longer reproduces, legitimate behavior remains intact, and relevant repository checks pass; preserve exact commands and results in the verification summary. Otherwise record `failed` and state the failing gate or proof gap. Do not close the finding.

When a parent thread delegates a remediation stage, the worker owns that stage through its terminal workbench update. The parent remains an orchestrator and must not duplicate the worker's edits or treat a chat response as completion.

## Outcome and Output Contract

In the final response, include:

- outcome: `fixed`, `no_change`, or `blocked`
- the concrete vulnerable path, security invariant, and legitimate behavior that had to remain
- the selected patch strategy and why it was the narrowest complete repository-native option, or the unresolved product decision when blocked
- files changed
- tests or validation artifacts added
- commands run and their pass, fail, or unknown results, grouped by the ordered verification gates
- explicit statement of how the original issue was shown not to reproduce
- explicit statement of how legitimate behavior was shown to remain intact
- remaining uncertainty or skipped validation, if any

If using a scan artifact directory, resolve it using `../../references/scan-artifacts.md`, then write a visible report to the fix report path. If there is no existing scan directory, a final chat summary is sufficient unless the user asks for a file.

## Hard Rules

- Do not report `fixed` until every ordered verification gate has passed. Omit a check only when repository evidence shows it is irrelevant; an unavailable relevant check makes verification `blocked` and must be reported.
- Do not rely only on code inspection when a focused test or reproducer is feasible.
- Do not broaden the patch into unrelated cleanup, sibling findings, or architectural redesign without evidence that the broader change is required for complete closure.
- Do not remove user changes or unrelated local modifications.
- Do not weaken authentication, authorization, tenant isolation, input validation, sandboxing, or logging to make tests pass.
- Do not hide proof gaps. If the environment blocks validation, say exactly which command or setup failed and what evidence is still missing.
